## `css/string-no-newline` — No line breaks inside selector strings

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-css` · `codelaw-rules-css` · **Languages:** CSS, SCSS
- **Fix:** `suggest` (the choices are a space or an escaped line break (`\A`) the string keeps; each makes a selector the browser drops today start to match, and only the author knows which was meant)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:css/recommended` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/css/string-no-newline.md

### What it checks

A string in a selector does not contain an unescaped line break. With the default options, strings in at-rule preludes and declaration values are not checked.

**Why:** A raw line break ends a CSS string early, so the selector is invalid and the rule is dropped.

### Options

| Option | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ignore` | `string[]` | `["at-rule-preludes", "declaration-values"]` | contexts not to check: `at-rule-preludes`, `declaration-values` |

### How to fix

1. Join the string onto one line, or escape the line break as `\A`.

### Examples

#### CSS

##### Don't

```css
[title="one
two"] {
  color: red;
}
```

##### Fixed (space)

```css
[title="one two"] {
  color: red;
}
```

##### Fixed (escape)

```css
[title="one\A two"] {
  color: red;
}
```

##### Do

```css
[title="one two"] {
  color: red;
}
```
#### SCSS

##### Don't

```scss
[title="one
two"] {
  color: red;
}
```

##### Fixed (space)

```scss
[title="one two"] {
  color: red;
}
```

##### Fixed (escape)

```scss
[title="one\A two"] {
  color: red;
}
```

##### Do

```scss
[title="one two"] {
  color: red;
}
```

## `css/syntax-string-no-invalid` — `@property` syntax strings are valid

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-css` · `codelaw-rules-css` · **Languages:** CSS, SCSS
- **Fix:** `suggest` (an unknown type name gets the names it is written for (`<size>` is `<length>` or `<length-percentage>`) or the names within two edits as choices, the first the default; `@property` is dropped today, so registering it changes behaviour. A string with another problem is manual, as the intended syntax is the author's call)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:css/recommended` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/css/syntax-string-no-invalid.md

### What it checks

The `syntax` of a `@property` rule is `"*"` or a `|`-separated list of supported `<type>` names and keywords, each with an optional `+` or `#`.

**Why:** A browser ignores a `@property` rule whose syntax is invalid, so the custom property is not registered.

### How to fix

1. Use a supported type name such as `<length>`, `<color>` or `<number>`.

### Examples

#### CSS

##### Don't

```css
@property --size {
  syntax: "<size>";
  inherits: false;
  initial-value: 0px;
}
```

##### Fixed (length)

```css
@property --size {
  syntax: "<length>";
  inherits: false;
  initial-value: 0px;
}
```

##### Fixed (length-percentage)

```css
@property --size {
  syntax: "<length-percentage>";
  inherits: false;
  initial-value: 0px;
}
```

##### Do

```css
@property --size {
  syntax: "<length>";
  inherits: false;
  initial-value: 0px;
}
```
#### SCSS

##### Don't

```scss
@property --size {
  syntax: "<size>";
  inherits: false;
  initial-value: 0px;
}
```

##### Fixed (length)

```scss
@property --size {
  syntax: "<length>";
  inherits: false;
  initial-value: 0px;
}
```

##### Fixed (length-percentage)

```scss
@property --size {
  syntax: "<length-percentage>";
  inherits: false;
  initial-value: 0px;
}
```

##### Do

```scss
@property --size {
  syntax: "<length>";
  inherits: false;
  initial-value: 0px;
}
```

## `css/todo-marker` — CSS TODO comments carry a ticket and, when asked, a date

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-css` · `codelaw-rules-css` · **Languages:** CSS
- **Fix:** `manual` (a ticket and a date are facts about the work that only the author knows; the engine can't invent them)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:css/markers` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/css/todo-marker.md

### What it checks

A comment line that opens with a marker tag (`TODO`, `FIXME`, `HACK` by default) in a `/* … */` comment carries a ticket, and a date when the project asks for one: `TODO(ABC-123, 2027-01-31): text`. The ticket and the date go in the parentheses, in either order, either one optional unless required; any other item in them (an owner's name) is ignored. The tag must start the comment line, so a sentence that merely mentions a TODO is not a marker.

A date that is written is always enforced, whether or not `require_date` is set: it is **expired** from the as-of date on (`--as-of`, `CODELAW_AS_OF`, else `HEAD`'s commit date, never the clock: [SR-BASELINE](https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/records/0104_baseline-and-deprecations.md) decision 9) and is a **warning** for the `warn_days` before it. A date that is not a calendar day is reported too. With no as-of date, only the missing and the malformed are reported.

**Why:** A TODO with no ticket has no owner and no place to be tracked, and one with no date never comes due; both outlive the people who wrote them. Naming a ticket ties the comment to the work, and a date makes the comment fail loudly the day it is overdue instead of rotting quietly.

**Configuration** is the `[todo]` table of `codelaw.toml` ([SR-CONFIG](https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/records/0110_config.md) decision 11a), one for every language:

```toml
[todo]
tags           = ["TODO", "FIXME", "HACK"]   # the words that open a marker
require_ticket = true                         # a ticket is required (default)
require_date   = false                        # a date is required (default: only a written date is enforced)
ticket_pattern = "[A-Z][A-Z0-9]+-\\d+"        # a whole ticket must match this regular expression
warn_days      = 14                           # warn this many days before the date
```

**A repo full of bare TODOs** gets every one of them at once. Take them into the baseline (`codelaw baseline`) and pay them down, or set `require_ticket = false` and let the rule enforce only the dates that are written.

### How to fix

1. Open or find the ticket for the work and write it in the parentheses: `TODO(ABC-123): …`.
2. When the project asks for a date (`require_date`), or the work has a deadline, add it: `TODO(ABC-123, 2027-01-31): …`.
3. For an expired marker: do the work and delete the comment; or, if the work really moves, change the date and say why in the text.
4. If the comment is not a to-do, rewrite it so it does not open with the tag.

### Examples

#### CSS

##### Don't

```css
/* FIXME: remove after the redesign */
.legacy { margin: 0; }
```

##### Do

```css
/* FIXME(UI-12): remove after the redesign */
.legacy { margin: 0; }
```

## `data/codeowners-coverage` — Every file has a code owner, and every CODEOWNERS pattern is live

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-data` · `codelaw-rules-data` · **Languages:** JSON, TOML
- **Fix:** `manual` (who owns a path is a decision about people; the finding names the paths and the lines, and the owner is the team's to choose)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:data/codeowners` at `warn`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/data/codeowners-coverage.md

### What it checks

CODEOWNERS routes each change to the people who should review it, so a file no pattern owns is a change nobody is asked about. This rule reads the project's CODEOWNERS file and its files — never a network — and reports three things: a file no pattern owns, a pattern that matches no file (stale), and a pattern that names no owner. The file is `[codeowners] path`, else the first that exists of `.github/CODEOWNERS`, `CODEOWNERS`, `docs/CODEOWNERS` and `.gitlab/CODEOWNERS`; a project with none gets no finding. GitHub's and GitLab's syntax both work: gitignore-style patterns, the last match wins, and GitLab's `[Section]` lines start a section (a file is owned when any section owns it).

CODEOWNERS is not one of codelaw's languages, so the findings sit on the project's root manifest — `package.json`, else `pyproject.toml`, else `codelaw.toml` — once per project, each naming the CODEOWNERS line. Unowned files are one finding that names up to ten paths and the count.

A pattern with no owner takes its paths out of ownership on purpose in GitHub's syntax; it is reported unless `[codeowners] allow_unowned = true`, which also keeps its paths out of the unowned list. `[codeowners] ignore` lists gitignore-style patterns of paths that need no owner, such as `*.lock`.

**Why:** A path with no owner is reviewed by whoever happens to look, and a stale pattern keeps an owner on the hook for code that moved, so the next file that lands there is owned by nobody and nothing says so.

### Options

| Option | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | `string` | *none* | the CODEOWNERS file, from the project root; by default the first that exists of .github/CODEOWNERS, CODEOWNERS, docs/CODEOWNERS and .gitlab/CODEOWNERS |
| `allow_unowned` | `boolean` | `false` | a pattern that names no owner is meant: it is not reported, and neither are its paths |
| `ignore` | `string[]` | `[]` | gitignore-style patterns of paths that need no owner, such as *.lock |

### How to fix

1. For an unowned path, add a pattern that covers it to the CODEOWNERS file (`/src/payments/ @org/payments`), or a catch-all `* @org/maintainers` first so every later pattern refines it.
2. For a stale pattern, delete the line, or correct the pattern to the folder or file it now means.
3. For a pattern with no owner, name one — or, if the path is meant to have none, set `[codeowners] allow_unowned = true`.
4. For paths that never need a review (lockfiles, generated files), list them in `[codeowners] ignore`.

### Examples

#### JSON

##### Don't

```json
// package.json
{
  "name": "app"
}
// src/a.js
// CODEOWNERS
/src/ @org/app
```

##### Do

```json
// package.json
{
  "name": "app"
}
// src/a.js
// CODEOWNERS
* @org/app
```

#### TOML

##### Don't

```toml
# pyproject.toml
[project]
name = "app"
# src/a.py
# CODEOWNERS
/src/ @org/app
```

##### Do

```toml
# pyproject.toml
[project]
name = "app"
# src/a.py
# CODEOWNERS
* @org/app
```

## `data/flag-registry` — The feature-flag registry is valid and holds only flags still read

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-data` · `codelaw-rules-data` · **Languages:** TOML
- **Fix:** `auto`
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** no preset
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/data/flag-registry.md

### What it checks

`.codelaw/flags.toml` registers each feature flag the code reads, with who owns it and when it goes:

```toml
[[flag]]
name    = "new-checkout"
owner   = "@payments"
ticket  = "PAY-123"
expires = "2027-02-28"   # a date, or "never" with a reason
keep    = "on"           # optional: the branch that stays — `js/flag-expiry` and `py/flag-expiry` collapse to it
reason  = "…"
```

The rule is on when the root config has a `[flags]` table (SR-PROJECT-GRAPH decision 11), and judges the registry once `[flags]` names a preset or an accessor. It reports, in the registry:

| an entry that | finding | fix |
|---|---|---|
| no read in the project names any more | `info` | `auto`: the entry is removed — `info`, uncertain and not removed while some read computes its flag's name |
| has no `name`, a key a flag does not have, or registers a flag twice | `error` | by hand |
| has no `expires`, one that is neither a date nor `never`, `never` without a `reason`, or `keep` other than `on`/`off` | `error` | by hand |
| — the file cannot be read as TOML | `error` | by hand |

**Why:** an entry for a flag the code no longer reads is a promise nobody keeps, and it hides the entries that matter.

### Options

| Option | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `presets` | `string[]` | *none* | `[flags] presets`, for this rule only: the SDKs whose reads codelaw knows (launchdarkly, unleash, split, openfeature, growthbook, flagsmith) |
| `accessors` | `string[]` | *none* | `[flags] accessors`, for this rule only: calls with one `$NAME` slot that read a flag |
| `inline` | `string` | *none* | `[flags] inline`, for this rule only: `allow` or `registry-only` |
| `warn_days` | `integer` | *none* | `[flags] warn_days`, for this rule only: how many days before `expires` a read warns |

### How to fix

1. Run `codelaw fix`: an entry with no read left is removed.
2. Otherwise edit the entry: give it a `name`, an `expires` date (or `never` and a `reason`), `keep = "on"` or `"off"` only, and no other keys.

### Examples

#### TOML

##### Don't

*With these options:* `{ accessors = ["isFeatureOn($NAME)"] }`

```toml files
# .codelaw/flags.toml
[[flag]]
name = "new-checkout"
owner = "@payments"
expires = "2027-02-28"

[[flag]]
name = "old-banner"
owner = "@web"
expires = "2026-06-30"
# src/checkout.js
export const on = isFeatureOn("new-checkout");
```

##### Do

*With these options:* `{ accessors = ["isFeatureOn($NAME)"] }`

```toml files
# .codelaw/flags.toml
[[flag]]
name = "new-checkout"
owner = "@payments"
expires = "2027-02-28"
# src/checkout.js
export const on = isFeatureOn("new-checkout");
```

## `deps/incomplete-scan` — Every advisory source was read

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-deps` · `codelaw-rules-deps` · **Languages:** JSON, TOML
- **Fix:** `manual` (reading an advisory source again needs the network, which the engine never uses (L5); turning a source off is the team's decision)
- **Severity when named:** `warn` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:deps/recommended` at `warn`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/deps/incomplete-scan.md

### What it checks

`.codelaw/deps-snapshot.json` records how each advisory source of `[deps] advisory_sources` answered the last `codelaw deps refresh`. While a source that is still enabled was `unavailable` — refused by a proxy, down, or a mirror that does not pass the audit endpoint through — the vulnerabilities only it knows are not reported, and this rule says so: one finding per project, naming each such source, its day and its error, on the root `package.json` (else the root `pyproject.toml`). A snapshot that holds packages but no source at all — written before the advisory sources, or with every source turned off — is reported too.

**Why:** A clean `deps/vulnerable` result means "no source we read knows of one"; when a source was not read, a clean result says less than it seems to.

### How to fix

1. Run `codelaw deps refresh` once the source is reachable, and commit the snapshot.
2. If the organisation will never allow that source, set `enabled = false` on it in `[deps] advisory_sources`, so the scan is complete as configured.

### Examples

#### JSON

##### Don't

```json
// .codelaw/deps-snapshot.json
{
  "fetched": "2026-10-29",
  "packages": {},
  "sources": {
    "osv": { "kind": "osv", "state": "unavailable", "on": "2026-10-29", "error": "https://api.osv.dev/v1/query answered HTTP 403" },
    "registry": { "kind": "registry", "state": "ok", "on": "2026-10-29" }
  }
}
// package.json
{
  "name": "app"
}
```

##### Do

```json
// .codelaw/deps-snapshot.json
{
  "fetched": "2026-10-29",
  "packages": {},
  "sources": {
    "osv": { "kind": "osv", "state": "ok", "on": "2026-10-29" },
    "registry": { "kind": "registry", "state": "ok", "on": "2026-10-29" }
  }
}
// package.json
{
  "name": "app"
}
```

#### TOML

##### Don't

```toml
# .codelaw/deps-snapshot.json
{
  "fetched": "2026-10-29",
  "packages": {},
  "sources": { "osv": { "kind": "osv", "state": "unavailable", "on": "2026-10-29", "error": "HTTP 403" } }
}
# pyproject.toml
[project]
name = "app"
```

##### Do

```toml
# .codelaw/deps-snapshot.json
{
  "fetched": "2026-10-29",
  "packages": {},
  "sources": { "osv": { "kind": "osv", "state": "ok", "on": "2026-10-29" } }
}
# pyproject.toml
[project]
name = "app"
```

## `deps/licence` — Every dependency has a licence the project allows

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-deps` · `codelaw-rules-deps` · **Languages:** JSON, TOML
- **Fix:** `manual` (replacing a package, or accepting its licence, is a legal and product decision no tool can make)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:deps/recommended` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/deps/licence.md

### What it checks

The licence of every version a project installs — each dependency of a `package.json` or `pyproject.toml`, and every package its lockfile installs through them — is read from `.codelaw/deps-snapshot.json`, where `codelaw deps refresh` keeps the registry's licence for each version in use, and judged against `[deps.licence]`. The rule reads only files, so `check` gives the same answer offline.

A licence is an **SPDX expression**: `MIT`, `(MIT OR Apache-2.0)`, `Apache-2.0 AND BSD-3-Clause`, `GPL-2.0-only WITH Classpath-exception-2.0`. `OR` needs one allowed alternative; `AND` needs every part allowed; `WITH` keeps its exception with its id. Free text such as `BSD` or `see LICENSE` is never guessed at: it is **unknown** (a short table of exact texts that name one licence without doubt, such as PyPI's `MIT License` classifier, is read as that licence).

Each id is judged by the configured lists first, then the defaults:

| list | default |
|---|---|
| `deny` | `GPL-*`, `AGPL-*`, `LGPL-*`, `SSPL-*`, `BUSL-*`, `EUPL-*` (copyleft and source-available) |
| `allow` | `MIT`, `Apache-2.0`, `BSD-2-Clause`, `BSD-3-Clause`, `ISC`, `0BSD`, `Unlicense`, `CC0-1.0`, `PSF-2.0`, `Python-2.0`, `BlueOak-1.0.0` |

```toml
[deps.licence]
allow = ["MPL-2.0", "LGPL-*"]        # globs over SPDX ids; lifts a default denial
deny = ["Unlicense"]
unknown = "warn"                     # error | warn | info | off
ignore = [{ package = "npm:some-gpl-tool", expires = "2027-01-01", reason = "dev-only, replaced in Q1" }]
```

A denied licence is reported at the rule's severity (`error`); an unknown one — on neither list, free text, or a direct dependency the registry names no licence for — at `[deps.licence] unknown`. A direct dependency's finding is on its manifest line. The transitive ones are one finding on the first line of the manifest beside the lockfile, naming up to ten packages and how many more, graded by the worst; for yarn classic each named package has a copy on its `yarn.lock` entry. `[deps] ignore` (whole packages) and `[deps.licence] ignore` hold a package.

**Why:** A copyleft licence deep in the tree can oblige the whole product; an unknown one is a question nobody has answered yet. Both are cheaper to answer when the package arrives than after it ships.

### How to fix

1. Read the package's licence. If the project can accept it, add its id to `[deps.licence] allow`.
2. Otherwise replace the package (or the dependency that brings it in), then run the install.
3. For a known exception, add a dated `[deps.licence] ignore` entry with `reason` and `added_by`.

### Examples

#### JSON

##### Don't

```json
// .codelaw/deps-snapshot.json
{
  "fetched": "2026-10-29",
  "packages": {
    "npm:gpl-lib": { "versions": { "1.0.0": "2024-01-01" }, "licence": { "1.0.0": "GPL-3.0-only" } }
  },
  "sources": { "osv": { "kind": "osv", "state": "ok", "on": "2026-10-29" } }
}
// package.json
{
  "dependencies": {
    "gpl-lib": "^1.0.0"
  }
}
```

##### Do

```json
// .codelaw/deps-snapshot.json
{
  "fetched": "2026-10-29",
  "packages": {
    "npm:mit-lib": { "versions": { "1.0.0": "2024-01-01" }, "licence": { "1.0.0": "MIT OR GPL-3.0-only" } }
  },
  "sources": { "osv": { "kind": "osv", "state": "ok", "on": "2026-10-29" } }
}
// package.json
{
  "dependencies": {
    "mit-lib": "^1.0.0"
  }
}
```

#### TOML

##### Don't

```toml
# .codelaw/deps-snapshot.json
{
  "fetched": "2026-10-29",
  "packages": {
    "pypi:odd": { "versions": { "2.0": "2024-01-01" }, "licence": { "2.0": "see LICENSE.txt" } }
  },
  "sources": { "osv": { "kind": "osv", "state": "ok", "on": "2026-10-29" } }
}
# pyproject.toml
[project]
name = "app"
dependencies = ["odd>=2.0"]
```

##### Do

```toml
# .codelaw/deps-snapshot.json
{
  "fetched": "2026-10-29",
  "packages": {
    "pypi:fine": { "versions": { "2.0": "2024-01-01" }, "licence": { "2.0": "Apache-2.0" } }
  },
  "sources": { "osv": { "kind": "osv", "state": "ok", "on": "2026-10-29" } }
}
# pyproject.toml
[project]
name = "app"
dependencies = ["fine>=2.0"]
```

## `deps/lockfile-sync` — The lockfile matches its manifest

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-deps` · `codelaw-rules-deps` · **Languages:** JSON, TOML
- **Fix:** `manual` (only the package manager can write its lockfile, and codelaw never runs installers)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:deps/recommended` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/deps/lockfile-sync.md

### What it checks

A manifest edited without running the install leaves a lockfile that installs something else: CI's `npm ci` refuses it, or a teammate gets a different tree. The rule compares each `package.json` and `pyproject.toml` with the lockfile that installs it — beside it, or a workspace's at the root — through what the lockfile records of the manifest it was made from:

| lockfile | what it records | reported |
|---|---|---|
| `package-lock.json` | `packages[""]` (a workspace's `packages["<dir>"]`): each dependency's range as written | missing, another range, a name the manifest dropped |
| `pnpm-lock.yaml` | `importers` (v5: `specifiers`): each `specifier` | missing, another range, a name the manifest dropped |
| `yarn.lock` | an entry per `name@range` (berry: `name@npm:range`) | a dependency with no entry |
| `uv.lock` | the project's `[package.metadata] requires-dist` and `requires-dev` | missing, another range, a name the manifest dropped |
| `poetry.lock` | `[metadata] content-hash`, a SHA-256 of the dependency tables | a hash that does not match, recomputed as Poetry 1.x and 2.x do |

A dependency's finding is on its manifest line; one about the whole file on its first line. The message names the command that brings the lockfile up to date: `npm install`, `pnpm install`, `yarn install`, `uv lock` or `poetry lock`. The rule reads only files and never edits a lockfile.

**Why:** The lockfile is what installs. A manifest it does not match says one thing and ships another.

### How to fix

1. Run the command the message names in the folder of the lockfile.
2. Commit the manifest and the lockfile together.

### Examples

#### JSON

##### Don't

```json
// package-lock.json
{
  "lockfileVersion": 3,
  "packages": {
    "": { "dependencies": { "react": "^18.2.0" } }
  }
}
// package.json
{
  "dependencies": {
    "react": "^18.3.1"
  }
}
```

##### Do

```json
// package-lock.json
{
  "lockfileVersion": 3,
  "packages": {
    "": { "dependencies": { "react": "^18.3.1" } }
  }
}
// package.json
{
  "dependencies": {
    "react": "^18.3.1"
  }
}
```

#### TOML

##### Don't

```toml
# uv.lock
version = 1

[[package]]
name = "app"
version = "0.1.0"
source = { virtual = "." }

[package.metadata]
requires-dist = [{ name = "requests", specifier = ">=2.31" }]
# pyproject.toml
[project]
name = "app"
dependencies = ["requests>=2.32"]
```

##### Do

```toml
# uv.lock
version = 1

[[package]]
name = "app"
version = "0.1.0"
source = { virtual = "." }

[package.metadata]
requires-dist = [{ name = "requests", specifier = ">=2.32" }]
# pyproject.toml
[project]
name = "app"
dependencies = ["requests>=2.32"]
```

## `deps/outdated` — Dependencies are on their latest version

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-deps` · `codelaw-rules-deps` · **Languages:** JSON, TOML
- **Fix:** `suggest` (a new major or minor version can change behaviour; the fix moves the range to the latest version, and the code that uses the package may need changes)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:deps/recommended` at `warn`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/deps/outdated.md

### What it checks

Each dependency of a `package.json` (`dependencies`, `devDependencies`, `peerDependencies`, `optionalDependencies`) and of a `pyproject.toml` (`[project] dependencies`, `[project.optional-dependencies]`, `[dependency-groups]`) is compared with `.codelaw/deps-snapshot.json`, the registry facts `codelaw deps refresh` wrote. The rule reads only that file and the lockfiles; it never reads a registry, so `check` gives the same answer offline. With no snapshot, nothing is reported.

The version in use is the lockfile's (`package-lock.json`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `yarn.lock`, `uv.lock` or `poetry.lock`, beside the manifest or above it), else the one the range starts from. The latest is the highest stable version in the snapshot — by semver for npm, PEP 440 for Python — that is not deprecated or yanked and is at least `[deps] min_release_age` old on the snapshot's `fetched` date.

Each finding is graded, and `[deps] severity` sets each grade's severity (or `off`):

| finding | default |
|---|---|
| a major version behind | `warn` |
| a minor or patch version behind | `info` |
| the version in use is deprecated (npm) or yanked (PyPI) | `error` |
| the range already allows the latest, but the lockfile is behind | `info` |

The fix moves the range's version to the latest and keeps its operator: `^`, `~`, `>=`, `=` or none for npm; `==`, `>=` or `~=` for Python, at the precision written (`~=4.2` becomes `~=5.1`). A range the fix can't move without changing its meaning — `||`, a hyphen, `x`, an upper bound the latest is outside — is reported without a fix. `[deps] ignore` names packages never reported.

**Why:** A dependency left behind stops getting fixes and security patches, and the jump grows with every release; a deprecated or yanked version was withdrawn by its own maintainers.

### How to fix

1. Run `codelaw fix --unsafe` to move the range to the latest version, or edit the version by hand.
2. Run your package manager's install (`npm install`, `uv lock`, …) so the lockfile follows.
3. For a major version, read the package's changelog and update the code that uses it.
4. If the project must stay on this version, add the package to `[deps] ignore`, with an `expires` date when the stay is temporary.

### Examples

#### JSON

##### Don't

```json
// .codelaw/deps-snapshot.json
{
  "fetched": "2026-10-25",
  "packages": {
    "npm:react": { "latest": "19.2.0", "versions": { "18.3.1": "2024-04-26", "19.2.0": "2025-10-01" } }
  }
}
// package.json
{
  "dependencies": {
    "react": "^18.3.1"
  }
}
```

##### Do

```json
// .codelaw/deps-snapshot.json
{
  "fetched": "2026-10-25",
  "packages": {
    "npm:react": { "latest": "19.2.0", "versions": { "18.3.1": "2024-04-26", "19.2.0": "2025-10-01" } }
  }
}
// package.json
{
  "dependencies": {
    "react": "^19.2.0"
  }
}
```

#### TOML

##### Don't

```toml
# .codelaw/deps-snapshot.json
{
  "fetched": "2026-10-25",
  "packages": {
    "pypi:django": { "latest": "5.1.2", "versions": { "4.2.0": "2023-04-03", "5.1.2": "2024-10-08" } }
  }
}
# pyproject.toml
[project]
name = "app"
dependencies = ["django~=4.2"]
```

##### Do

```toml
# .codelaw/deps-snapshot.json
{
  "fetched": "2026-10-25",
  "packages": {
    "pypi:django": { "latest": "5.1.2", "versions": { "4.2.0": "2023-04-03", "5.1.2": "2024-10-08" } }
  }
}
# pyproject.toml
[project]
name = "app"
dependencies = ["django~=5.1"]
```

## `deps/runtime-agreement` — Every place that names the Node or Python version agrees

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-deps` · `codelaw-rules-deps` · **Languages:** JSON, TOML, YAML
- **Fix:** `suggest` (changing a runtime pin changes what CI, the container or a developer's shell runs; the agreed version may not be the one the team meant)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:deps/recommended` at `warn`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/deps/runtime-agreement.md

### What it checks

A project names its runtime in many places, and they drift: CI tests Node 18, the container runs 20, `engines` says 22. The rule reads, at the project root:

| | Node | Python |
|---|---|---|
| the range | `engines.node` in `package.json` | `requires-python` in `pyproject.toml` |
| pins | `volta.node`, `.nvmrc`, `.node-version`, `.tool-versions` (`nodejs`), `mise.toml` `[tools] node`, `actions/setup-node`'s `node-version` in `.github/workflows/*.yml`, `Dockerfile` `FROM node:<tag>` | `.python-version`, `.tool-versions` (`python`), `mise.toml` `[tools] python`, `actions/setup-python`'s `python-version`, `FROM python:<tag>` |

Every pin must be **inside the range** and **agree with the others**: `20` agrees with `20.11.1`; `20.10` does not. An alias (`lts/*`, `latest`) or an expression (`${{ matrix.node }}`) is not read. The pin the others are compared with is the first, in the order above, that the range allows — or the source `[deps.runtime] source` names:

```toml
[deps.runtime]
source = { node = ".nvmrc", python = "requires-python" }   # the truth; defaults engines.node, requires-python
```

Where it is reported, and the fix:

- **A pin in `package.json`, `mise.toml` or a workflow:** on the pin, and the fix sets it to the agreed version at the precision it was written.
- **A pin in `.nvmrc`, `.node-version`, `.python-version`, `.tool-versions` or the `Dockerfile`:** on the root `package.json` (Node) or `pyproject.toml` (Python) — on the range when it names one — and on the pin's own line; change it by hand: codelaw never edits those files.
- **A range that does not allow the pin `[deps.runtime] source` names:** on the range, to widen by hand.

**Why:** The version CI tests is the only one known to work; every other place should name the same one.

### How to fix

1. Run `codelaw fix --unsafe` to move the pins in `package.json`, `mise.toml` and the workflows to the agreed version.
2. Edit the version files and the `Dockerfile`'s `FROM` line to the same version by hand.
3. If the range is what is wrong, widen `engines.node` or `requires-python`.

### Examples

#### JSON

##### Don't

```json
// .nvmrc
20.11.1
// package.json
{
  "engines": { "node": ">=20.11" },
  "volta": { "node": "18.19.0" }
}
```

##### Do

```json
// .nvmrc
20.11.1
// package.json
{
  "engines": { "node": ">=20.11" },
  "volta": { "node": "20.11.1" }
}
```

#### YAML

##### Don't

```yaml
# .nvmrc
20
# .github/workflows/ci.yml
on: push
jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 18
```

##### Do

```yaml
# .nvmrc
20
# .github/workflows/ci.yml
on: push
jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20
```

#### TOML

##### Don't

```toml
# .python-version
3.12
# pyproject.toml
[project]
name = "app"
requires-python = ">=3.11"
# mise.toml
[tools]
python = "3.10"
```

##### Do

```toml
# .python-version
3.12
# pyproject.toml
[project]
name = "app"
requires-python = ">=3.11"
# mise.toml
[tools]
python = "3.12"
```

## `deps/stale-snapshot` — The dependency snapshot is recent

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-deps` · `codelaw-rules-deps` · **Languages:** JSON, TOML
- **Fix:** `manual` (refreshing the snapshot reads the registries, which needs the network; the engine never uses it (L5))
- **Severity when named:** `info` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:deps/recommended` at `info`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/deps/stale-snapshot.md

### What it checks

`.codelaw/deps-snapshot.json` — the registry facts `deps/outdated` reads — was fetched no more than `[deps] max_snapshot_age` (14 days by default) before the as-of date, and can be read. The finding is on the root `package.json`, or the root `pyproject.toml` when there is no root `package.json`, so a project gets one. The age is judged on the as-of date (`--as-of`, `CODELAW_AS_OF`, else `HEAD`'s commit date), never the clock; with no as-of date, only an unreadable snapshot is reported.

**Why:** An old snapshot hides every release since it was written, so `deps/outdated` says a dependency is current when it isn't.

### How to fix

1. Run `codelaw deps refresh`: it reads npm and the Python index and writes the snapshot again.
2. Commit `.codelaw/deps-snapshot.json`, so CI and every teammate judge by the same facts.

### Examples

#### JSON

##### Don't

```json
// .codelaw/deps-snapshot.json
{ "fetched": "2026-10-25", "packages": [ }
// package.json
{
  "name": "app"
}
```

##### Do

```json
// .codelaw/deps-snapshot.json
{ "fetched": "2026-10-25", "packages": {} }
// package.json
{
  "name": "app"
}
```

#### TOML

##### Don't

```toml
# .codelaw/deps-snapshot.json
{ "fetched": "2026-10-25", "packages": [ }
# pyproject.toml
[project]
name = "app"
```

##### Do

```toml
# .codelaw/deps-snapshot.json
{ "fetched": "2026-10-25", "packages": {} }
# pyproject.toml
[project]
name = "app"
```

## `deps/version-drift` — A monorepo declares each dependency with one range

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-deps` · `codelaw-rules-deps` · **Languages:** JSON, TOML
- **Fix:** `suggest` (aligning a range changes what that workspace installs; the lower range may be on purpose)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:deps/recommended` at `warn`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/deps/version-drift.md

### What it checks

In a monorepo — npm, yarn or pnpm workspaces (`package.json` `workspaces`, `pnpm-workspace.yaml` `packages`), or a uv workspace (`[tool.uv.workspace] members`) — the same dependency declared with different ranges in different workspaces installs two versions, or one version some workspace was never tested with. The rule compares each dependency's range across the root manifest and every member: `dependencies`, `devDependencies` and `optionalDependencies` (never `peerDependencies`, which are wide on purpose), and `[project] dependencies`, `optional-dependencies` and `[dependency-groups]` (PyPI ranges by their clauses, so `>= 2.31` and `>=2.31.0` agree). A range with a protocol (`workspace:`, `file:`, a URL) is not compared.

Each manifest whose range is not the target gets a finding, and the fix rewrites it to the target:

```toml
[deps.drift]
policy = "highest"          # the range whose floor is highest (default); "root": the root manifest's
ignore = ["npm:typescript"] # never compared
```

**Why:** One version per dependency is one set of bugs, one set of types and one upgrade.

### How to fix

1. Run `codelaw fix --unsafe` to align the range, or edit it by hand.
2. Run the install so the lockfile follows.
3. If a workspace needs another version on purpose, add the package to `[deps.drift] ignore`.

### Examples

#### JSON

##### Don't

```json
// package.json
{
  "private": true,
  "workspaces": ["packages/*"]
}
// packages/web/package.json
{
  "dependencies": {
    "react": "^18.2.0"
  }
}
// packages/app/package.json
{
  "dependencies": {
    "react": "^18.3.1"
  }
}
```

##### Do

```json
// package.json
{
  "private": true,
  "workspaces": ["packages/*"]
}
// packages/web/package.json
{
  "dependencies": {
    "react": "^18.3.1"
  }
}
// packages/app/package.json
{
  "dependencies": {
    "react": "^18.3.1"
  }
}
```

#### TOML

##### Don't

```toml
# pyproject.toml
[project]
name = "mono"
dependencies = ["httpx>=0.27"]

[tool.uv.workspace]
members = ["libs/*"]
# libs/core/pyproject.toml
[project]
name = "core"
dependencies = ["httpx>=0.25"]
```

##### Do

```toml
# pyproject.toml
[project]
name = "mono"
dependencies = ["httpx>=0.27"]

[tool.uv.workspace]
members = ["libs/*"]
# libs/core/pyproject.toml
[project]
name = "core"
dependencies = ["httpx>=0.27"]
```

## `deps/vulnerable` — No dependency in use has a known vulnerability

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-deps` · `codelaw-rules-deps` · **Languages:** JSON, TOML
- **Fix:** `suggest` (the fix moves a range or adds an override to the lowest known-clean version, which changes what installs; a new major can change behaviour, and an override changes the install of the whole tree)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:deps/recommended` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/deps/vulnerable.md

### What it checks

Every version a project installs — each dependency of a `package.json` or `pyproject.toml`, and every package its lockfile (`package-lock.json`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `yarn.lock`, `uv.lock`, `poetry.lock`) installs through them — is compared with the advisories in `.codelaw/deps-snapshot.json`, which `codelaw deps refresh` wrote from the enabled `[deps] advisory_sources`. The rule reads only that file and the lockfiles; it never reads the network, so `check` gives the same answer offline. With no snapshot, or one that holds no advisories, nothing is reported (`deps/incomplete-scan` says why).

The finding names the worst advisory, its severity and CVE, how many more there are, and the version to move to: the **lowest known-clean** version above the one in use — a version no merged advisory affects and an advisory source covered — that is not deprecated or yanked and is at least `[deps] min_release_age` old, **inside the major in use first**. When the major has none, the lowest clean version above it is offered and the message says it is a new major. A fixed version no source covered is named but never offered ("not verified clean"); with no fixed version at all, the fix is manual.

Each finding is graded by its worst advisory, and `[deps] severity` sets each grade's severity (or `off`):

| advisory severity | default |
|---|---|
| `critical`, `high` | `error` |
| `moderate` | `warn` |
| `low` | `info` |

An advisory no source grades counts as `high`.

Where it is reported, and the fix:

- **A direct dependency:** on its line in the manifest; the fix moves the range's version to the target and keeps its operator (`^`, `~`, `>=`, `=` or none; `==`, `>=` or `~=`).
- **A transitive one:** on the first line of the manifest beside the lockfile — where the override that fixes it is written — and the fix adds that override at the exact target: npm `overrides`, `pnpm.overrides`, yarn `resolutions`, uv's `[tool.uv] override-dependencies`. A lockfile is never edited. An override already in the manifest is the version the next install takes: a clean one settles the finding, a vulnerable one is reported with the version to change it to. A yarn classic finding has a copy on its `yarn.lock` entry.
- **In `poetry.lock`:** Poetry has no override, so the message says to add a direct constraint.

Every message ends with the install to run (`npm install`, `uv lock`, …) and the snapshot's day, and says `incomplete` while an enabled source was unavailable. `[deps] ignore` takes a package, or `{ package, advisory, expires, added_by, reason }` for one advisory until a date.

**Why:** A vulnerable version stays exploitable until someone moves it, and the version that fixes one advisory can carry another; the lowest version every source leaves clean is the smallest safe change.

### How to fix

1. Run `codelaw fix --unsafe` to move the range (or add the override) to the version named, or make the same edit by hand.
2. Run the install the message names (`npm install`, `pnpm install`, `yarn install`, `uv lock`, `poetry lock`) so the lockfile follows; codelaw never runs installers.
3. For a new major, read the package's changelog and update the code that uses it.
4. With no clean version: replace the package, remove it, or add a dated `[deps] ignore` entry naming the advisory, with a reason.

### Examples

#### JSON

##### Don't

```json
// .codelaw/deps-snapshot.json
{
  "fetched": "2026-10-29",
  "packages": {
    "npm:lodash": {
      "versions": { "4.17.15": "2019-07-19", "4.17.21": "2021-02-20" },
      "advisories": [ { "id": "GHSA-35jh-r3h4-6jhm", "aliases": ["CVE-2021-23337"], "severity": "high", "affected": ["<4.17.21"], "fixed": ["4.17.21"], "sources": ["osv"] } ],
      "scanned": { "osv": ["*"] }
    }
  },
  "sources": { "osv": { "kind": "osv", "state": "ok", "on": "2026-10-29" } }
}
// package.json
{
  "dependencies": {
    "lodash": "^4.17.15"
  }
}
```

##### Do

```json
// .codelaw/deps-snapshot.json
{
  "fetched": "2026-10-29",
  "packages": {
    "npm:lodash": {
      "versions": { "4.17.15": "2019-07-19", "4.17.21": "2021-02-20" },
      "advisories": [ { "id": "GHSA-35jh-r3h4-6jhm", "aliases": ["CVE-2021-23337"], "severity": "high", "affected": ["<4.17.21"], "fixed": ["4.17.21"], "sources": ["osv"] } ],
      "scanned": { "osv": ["*"] }
    }
  },
  "sources": { "osv": { "kind": "osv", "state": "ok", "on": "2026-10-29" } }
}
// package.json
{
  "dependencies": {
    "lodash": "^4.17.21"
  }
}
```

#### TOML

##### Don't

```toml
# .codelaw/deps-snapshot.json
{
  "fetched": "2026-10-29",
  "packages": {
    "pypi:jinja2": {
      "versions": { "3.1.2": "2022-04-28", "3.1.3": "2024-01-10" },
      "advisories": [ { "id": "GHSA-h5c8-rqwp-cp95", "severity": "moderate", "affected": ["<3.1.3"], "fixed": ["3.1.3"], "sources": ["osv"] } ],
      "scanned": { "osv": ["*"] }
    }
  },
```

## `django/django-all-with-model-form` — ModelForm does not use fields = '__all__'

- **Pack:** `codelaw-rules-django` · **Languages:** Python
- **Fix:** `manual` (the fields to list are the author's)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:django/recommended` at `warn`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/django/django-all-with-model-form.md

### What it checks

A `ModelForm`'s `Meta` does not set `fields = "__all__"`.

**Why:** Every model field, including ones added later, becomes user-editable without anyone deciding so.

### How to fix

1. Set `fields` to the list of fields the form shows.

### Examples

#### Python

##### Don't

```python
class BookForm(forms.ModelForm):
    class Meta:
        model = Book
        fields = '__all__'
```

##### Do

```python
class BookForm(forms.ModelForm):
    class Meta:
        model = Book
        fields = ['title', 'author']
```

## `django/django-exclude-with-model-form` — ModelForm lists fields, not exclude

- **Pack:** `codelaw-rules-django` · **Languages:** Python
- **Fix:** `manual` (the fields to list are the author's)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:django/recommended` at `warn`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/django/django-exclude-with-model-form.md

### What it checks

A `ModelForm`'s `Meta` names the fields it uses in `fields`, not the ones it leaves out in `exclude`.

**Why:** With `exclude`, a field added to the model later appears in the form — and is writable by users — without anyone deciding so.

### How to fix

1. Replace `exclude` with `fields = [...]` naming each field the form shows.

### Examples

#### Python

##### Don't

```python
class BookForm(forms.ModelForm):
    class Meta:
        model = Book
        exclude = ['owner']
```

##### Do

```python
class BookForm(forms.ModelForm):
    class Meta:
        model = Book
        fields = ['title', 'author']
```

## `django/django-locals-in-render-function` — No locals() as a template context

- **Pack:** `codelaw-rules-django` · **Languages:** Python
- **Fix:** `manual` (the context's keys are the author's to list)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:django/recommended` at `warn`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/django/django-locals-in-render-function.md

### What it checks

`render()` is not passed `locals()` as its context.

**Why:** It sends every local variable to the template, hiding what the template uses and leaking more than it needs.

### How to fix

1. Pass a dict of the names the template uses.

### Examples

#### Python

##### Don't

```python
def view(request):
    items = load()
    return render(request, 'list.html', locals())
```

##### Do

```python
def view(request):
    items = load()
    return render(request, 'list.html', {'items': items})
```

## `django/django-model-without-dunder-str` — A model defines __str__

- **Pack:** `codelaw-rules-django` · **Languages:** Python
- **Fix:** `manual` (what represents the object is the author's to choose)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:django/recommended` at `warn`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/django/django-model-without-dunder-str.md

### What it checks

A concrete Django model defines `__str__`.

**Why:** Without it the admin, the shell and error messages show `Book object (1)`.

### How to fix

1. Add `def __str__(self): return self.<name field>`.

### Examples

#### Python

##### Don't

```python
class Book(models.Model):
    title = models.CharField(max_length=80)
```

##### Do

```python
class Book(models.Model):
    title = models.CharField(max_length=80)

    def __str__(self):
        return self.title
```

## `django/django-non-leading-receiver-decorator` — @receiver is the first decorator

- **Pack:** `codelaw-rules-django` · **Languages:** Python
- **Fix:** `suggest` (swapping the two decorators changes which function is connected; the reviewer confirms the wrapper order was not deliberate (offered only when `@receiver` is the second of exactly those two))
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:django/recommended` at `warn`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/django/django-non-leading-receiver-decorator.md

### What it checks

`@receiver` is the outermost (first) decorator of a signal handler.

**Why:** Django connects whatever `@receiver` wraps; below another decorator it connects the undecorated function and the other decorator never runs.

### How to fix

1. Move `@receiver(...)` to the top of the decorator list.

### Examples

#### Python

##### Don't

```python
@transaction.atomic
@receiver(post_save, sender=Book)
def on_save(sender, **kwargs):
    pass
```

##### Do

```python
@receiver(post_save, sender=Book)
@transaction.atomic
def on_save(sender, **kwargs):
    pass
```

## `django/django-nullable-model-string-field` — No null=True on string fields

- **Pack:** `codelaw-rules-django` · **Languages:** Python
- **Fix:** `manual` (removing `null=True` needs a migration and a default for the existing NULLs)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:django/recommended` at `warn`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/django/django-nullable-model-string-field.md

### What it checks

A Django string field (`CharField`, `TextField`, `SlugField`, `EmailField`, …) does not set `null=True`.

**Why:** A string field then has two empty values, `NULL` and `''`; Django's convention is the empty string.

### How to fix

1. Remove `null=True` (keep `blank=True` if the field is optional) and migrate existing NULLs to `''`.

### Examples

#### Python

##### Don't

```python
class Book(models.Model):
    title = models.CharField(max_length=80, null=True)
```

##### Do

```python
class Book(models.Model):
    title = models.CharField(max_length=80, blank=True)
```

## `django/django-unordered-body-content-in-model` — A model's body follows Django's order

- **Pack:** `codelaw-rules-django` · **Languages:** Python
- **Fix:** `suggest` (the field moves above the methods before it, one method a pass, keeping the fields' own order; a comment above the field stays where it was)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:django/recommended` at `warn`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/django/django-unordered-body-content-in-model.md

### What it checks

Inside a model, fields come before `class Meta`, and both before the methods.

**Why:** Django's style guide orders a model as fields, custom managers, `Meta`, `__str__`, `save`, `get_absolute_url`, then other methods, so every model reads the same way.

### How to fix

1. Move the fields to the top of the class and `class Meta` after them, before any method.

### Examples

#### Python

##### Don't

```python
class Book(models.Model):
    def __str__(self):
        return self.title

    title = models.CharField(max_length=80)
```

##### Do

```python
class Book(models.Model):
    title = models.CharField(max_length=80)

    def __str__(self):
        return self.title
```

### Differences from the source

Fields and `Meta` after a method are reported; the source also orders managers, `__str__`, `save` and `get_absolute_url` among themselves.

## `fastapi/fast-api-non-annotated-dependency` — Dependencies through Annotated

- **Pack:** `codelaw-rules-fastapi` · **Languages:** Python
- **Fix:** `suggest` (the suggestion uses `Annotated`, which the file must import from `typing`)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:fastapi/recommended` at `warn`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/fastapi/fast-api-non-annotated-dependency.md

### What it checks

A route parameter's `Depends`, `Query`, `Path`, `Body`, `Header`, `Cookie`, `Form`, `File` or `Security` is written in `Annotated[...]`, not as the default value.

**Why:** FastAPI recommends `Annotated`: the parameter keeps a real default, the function stays callable outside FastAPI, and the dependency can be reused as a type.

### Examples

#### Python

##### Don't

```python
async def read(db: Session = Depends(get_db)):
    return db
```

##### Do

```python
async def read(db: Annotated[Session, Depends(get_db)]):
    return db
```

## `fastapi/fast-api-redundant-response-model` — No response_model that repeats the return annotation

- **Pack:** `codelaw-rules-fastapi` · **Languages:** Python
- **Fix:** `auto`
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:fastapi/recommended` at `warn`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/fastapi/fast-api-redundant-response-model.md

### What it checks

A route does not pass `response_model=` equal to its function's return annotation.

**Why:** FastAPI reads the response model from the return annotation; repeating it is noise that can drift.

### Examples

#### Python

##### Don't

```python
@app.get("/items", response_model=Item)
async def read() -> Item:
    return Item()
```

##### Do

```python
@app.get("/items")
async def read() -> Item:
    return Item()
```

##### Fixed

```python
@app.get("/items")
async def read() -> Item:
    return Item()
```

## `graph/no-unused-css-classes` — CSS classes must be used somewhere

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-css` · `codelaw-rules-css` · **Languages:** CSS
- **Fix:** `suggest` (A class can be built at run time or used by markup outside the repo, so removing its rule needs a human or agent to accept the diff.)
- **Severity when named:** `warn` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:css/project` at `warn`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/graph/no-unused-css-classes.md

### What it checks

Every class a stylesheet defines appears in the project's HTML, JSX, templates or strings.

**Why:** a rule for a class no markup uses is dead weight every page downloads, and it makes the stylesheet harder to change safely.

### How to fix

1. Search for the class: a name built at run time (`"btn-" + kind`) counts only through its static prefix.
2. If markup outside the repo uses it, add the file to `[graph] keep` or list it in the package's `style` or `exports`.
3. Otherwise delete the rule, or the class from its selector list.

### Examples

#### CSS

##### Don't

```css files
/* src/styles.css */
.card { padding: 1rem; }
.legacy-banner { color: red; }
<!-- index.html -->
<div class="card"></div>
```

##### Do

```css files
/* src/styles.css */
.card { padding: 1rem; }
<!-- index.html -->
<div class="card"></div>
```

## `graph/no-unused-exports` — Exported symbols must be used somewhere

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-js` · `codelaw-rules-js` · `codelaw-rules-python` · **Languages:** JavaScript, JSX, TypeScript, TSX, Python
- **Fix:** `suggest` (Static analysis can't rule out reflective or external use, so removal needs a human or agent to accept the diff.)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:js/project` at `error` · `codelaw:py/project` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/graph/no-unused-exports.md

### What it checks

Every exported symbol is imported by another module, is reachable from an entry point, or is marked `@public` / `@keep`.

**Why:** an export nothing imports is dead code that still looks like API: readers keep it, refactors carry it, and it hides what a module is really for.

### How to fix

1. Run `codelaw graph why-unused <symbol>` (`<file>#<export>` or `<module>:<name>`) to see each entry, keep and import clause.
2. If something outside the repo uses it, add the file to `[graph] entry` or `[graph] keep`, add its decorator to `[graph] registrars`, or tag it `/** @public */` / `# codelaw: keep`.
3. Otherwise delete the declaration (and its `__all__` or `export { … }` entry), or drop `export` if its own file still uses it.

### Examples

#### JavaScript

##### Don't

```js files
// src/date.js
export function formatDate(d) { return d.toISOString(); }
export function parseDate(s) { return new Date(s); }
// src/app.js
import { formatDate } from "./date";
console.log(formatDate(new Date()));
```

##### Do

```js files
// src/date.js
export function formatDate(d) { return d.toISOString(); }
// src/app.js
import { formatDate } from "./date";
console.log(formatDate(new Date()));
```

#### JSX

##### Don't

```jsx files
// src/Button.jsx
export function Button() { return <button />; }
export function Unused() { return <span />; }
// src/App.jsx
import { Button } from "./Button";
console.log(<Button />);
```

##### Do

```jsx files
// src/Button.jsx
export function Button() { return <button />; }
// src/App.jsx
import { Button } from "./Button";
console.log(<Button />);
```

#### TypeScript

##### Don't

```ts files
// packages/utils/src/date.ts
export function formatDate(d: Date) { return d.toISOString(); }
export function parseDate(s: string) { return new Date(s); }
// packages/web/src/app.ts
import { formatDate } from "../../utils/src/date";
console.log(formatDate(new Date()));
```

##### Do

```ts files
// packages/utils/src/date.ts
export function formatDate(d: Date) { return d.toISOString(); }
// packages/web/src/app.ts
import { formatDate } from "../../utils/src/date";
console.log(formatDate(new Date()));
```

#### TSX

##### Don't

```tsx files
// src/theme.tsx
export const theme = { dark: false };
export const unusedTheme = { dark: true };
// src/main.tsx
import { theme } from "./theme";
console.log(theme);
```

##### Do

```tsx files
// src/theme.tsx
export const theme = { dark: false };
// src/main.tsx
import { theme } from "./theme";
console.log(theme);
```

#### Python

##### Don't

```py files
# app/dates.py
def format_date(d):
    return d.isoformat()
def parse_date(s):
    return s
# app/main.py
from app.dates import format_date
print(format_date(None))
```

##### Do

```py files
# app/dates.py
def format_date(d):
    return d.isoformat()
# app/main.py
from app.dates import format_date
print(format_date(None))
```

## `html/allowed-links` — Only the kinds of link the project allows

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-html` · `codelaw-rules-html` · **Languages:** HTML
- **Fix:** `manual` (which address to link to is the author's to write)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** no preset
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/html/allowed-links.md

### What it checks

With `allow_external`, `allow_relative` or `allow_absolute` set to `false`, links and sources of that kind are reported. All three are `true` by default, so the rule does nothing until one is turned off.

**Why:** A site served from several paths needs relative links, or none.

### Options

| Option | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `allow_external` | `boolean` | `true` | links to other origins |
| `allow_relative` | `boolean` | `true` | `a/b` links |
| `allow_absolute` | `boolean` | `true` | `/a/b` links |

### How to fix

1. Rewrite the address in an allowed form.

### Examples

#### HTML

##### Don't

*With these options:* `{ allow_external = false }`

```html
<a href="https://example.com/">x</a>
```

##### Do

*With these options:* `{ allow_external = false }`

```html
<a href="/x">x</a>
```

## `html/area-alt` — Image-map areas with a link have alt text

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-html` · `codelaw-rules-html` · **Languages:** HTML
- **Fix:** `manual` (the text that describes the area needs a human)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:html/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:html/a11y` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/html/area-alt.md

### What it checks

An `<area>` with `href` has non-empty `alt` text, and an `<area>` without `href` has no `alt`.

**Why:** A screen reader announces a linked area by its `alt`; without it the link has no name.

### Options

| Option | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `accessible` | `boolean` | `true` | require `alt` on every linked area, not just one area per link target |

### How to fix

1. Give each linked `<area>` an `alt` that says where it leads.
2. Remove `alt` from an `<area>` that has no `href`.

### Examples

#### HTML

##### Don't

```html
<img src="floor.png" usemap="#floor" alt="Floor plan">
<map name="floor">
  <area shape="rect" coords="0,0,50,50" href="/kitchen">
</map>
```

##### Do

```html
<img src="floor.png" usemap="#floor" alt="Floor plan">
<map name="floor">
  <area shape="rect" coords="0,0,50,50" href="/kitchen" alt="Kitchen">
</map>
```

## `html/aria-hidden-body` — <body> is not aria-hidden

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-html` · `codelaw-rules-html` · **Languages:** HTML
- **Fix:** `suggest` (removing it exposes the page to screen readers again, which changes what users hear)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:html/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:html/a11y` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/html/aria-hidden-body.md

### What it checks

`<body>` does not have `aria-hidden="true"`.

**Why:** It hides the whole page from assistive technology, while sighted users still see it.

### Examples

#### HTML

##### Don't

```html
<body aria-hidden="true">
  <p>Welcome</p>
</body>
```

##### Do

```html
<body>
  <p>Welcome</p>
</body>
```

## `html/aria-label-misuse` — aria-label is used only where it names something

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-html` · `codelaw-rules-html` · **Languages:** HTML
- **Fix:** `suggest` (the choices are removing the label, which nothing reads, or `role="img"`, which gives the element a name to carry; which was meant is the reviewer's call)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:html/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:html/a11y` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/html/aria-label-misuse.md

### What it checks

`aria-label` and `aria-labelledby` appear only on elements that can carry an accessible name: interactive and labelable elements, landmarks, elements with a `role` or `tabindex`, and a few others (`img`, `table`, `fieldset`, `dialog`, …).

**Why:** On a plain `<span>` or `<div>` screen readers ignore the label, so the text never reaches the user.

### Options

| Option | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `allowAnyNamable` | `boolean` | `false` | accept the label on any element ARIA lets be named, even where support is poor |

### How to fix

1. If the element acts as a control, use the matching element (`<button>`, `<a href>`) or add a `role`.
2. Otherwise put the text in the content, where everyone can read it, and remove the attribute.

### Examples

#### HTML

##### Don't

```html
<span aria-label="Close">×</span>
```

##### Fixed (remove)

```html
<span>×</span>
```

##### Fixed (role img)

```html
<span role="img" aria-label="Close">×</span>
```

##### Do

```html
<button type="button" aria-label="Close">×</button>
```

## `html/attr-pattern` — Attribute names follow the project's pattern

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-html` · `codelaw-rules-html` · **Languages:** HTML

### What it checks

An attribute's name matches `pattern` (lowercase letters, digits, `-` and `:` by default).

**Why:** Consistent attribute names are easy to search for.

### Options

| Option | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `pattern` | `string` | `"^[a-z0-9-:]+$"` | a regular expression attribute names must match |

### How to fix

1. Rename the attribute.

### Examples

#### HTML

##### Don't

```html

```

##### Do

