- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/scss/at-import-partial-extension-allowed-list.md

### What it checks

An `@import`'s file extension is in `list`. With no option set, the rule does nothing.

**Why:** A project loads its partials one way.

### Options

| Option | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `list` | `string[]` | `[]` | the extensions allowed |

### How to fix

1. Use an allowed extension, or none.

### Examples

#### SCSS

##### Don't

*With these options:* `{ list = ["scss"] }`

```scss
@import "a.sass";
```

##### Do

*With these options:* `{ list = ["scss"] }`

```scss
@import "a.scss";
```

## `scss/at-mixin-no-risky-nesting-selector` — No `&` after another selector inside a mixin

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-scss` · `codelaw-rules-scss` · **Languages:** SCSS
- **Fix:** `manual` (what the mixin's rule should match depends on where it is included)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** no preset
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/scss/at-mixin-no-risky-nesting-selector.md

### What it checks

Inside a `@mixin`, a nested rule's selector doesn't put `&` after another selector (`.dark &`).

**Why:** What it matches then depends on every place the mixin is included.

### How to fix

1. Pass the context in as an argument, or move the rule out of the mixin.

### Examples

#### SCSS

##### Don't

```scss
@mixin m {
  .dark & {
    color: red;
  }
}
```

##### Do

```scss
@mixin m {
  &.dark {
    color: red;
  }
}
```

## `scss/at-mixin-pattern` — Mixin names are kebab-case

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-scss` · `codelaw-rules-scss` · **Languages:** SCSS
- **Fix:** `manual` (renaming must update every `@include` of the mixin)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:scss/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/scss/at-mixin-pattern.md

### What it checks

Mixin names match a pattern, kebab-case by default.

**Why:** A consistent scheme makes names predictable across a codebase.

### Options

| Option | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `pattern` | `string` | `"^[a-z][a-z0-9]*(-[a-z0-9]+)*$"` | a regular expression a mixin name must match |

### How to fix

1. Rename the mixin to match the pattern.
2. Rename every `@include` of it.

### Examples

#### SCSS

##### Don't

```scss
@mixin ButtonBase {
  color: red;
}
```

##### Do

```scss
@mixin button-base {
  color: red;
}
```

### Differences from the source

Only the definition is checked.

## `scss/at-rule-no-unknown` — No unknown at-rules (SCSS)

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-scss` · `codelaw-rules-scss` · **Languages:** SCSS
- **Fix:** `suggest` (the known CSS and Sass at-rules within two edits are offered as choices, nearest first; a name with none near is manual)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:scss/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:scss/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/scss/at-rule-no-unknown.md

### What it checks

Every at-rule is one CSS or Sass defines: `@mixin`, `@include`, `@use`, `@if`, `@each` and the rest of Sass's own are known. This rule replaces `css/at-rule-no-unknown` on `.scss` files, which does not know Sass.

**Why:** A browser skips a CSS at-rule it does not know, block and all, and Sass passes an unknown one through, so a typo silently disables its contents.

### Options

| Option | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ignoreAtRules` | `string[]` | `[]` | at-rules to accept, such as a framework's; `/regex/` for a pattern |

### How to fix

1. Correct the at-rule name.
2. If a build tool handles it, add it to `ignoreAtRules`.

### Examples

#### SCSS

##### Don't

```scss
@mixn button {
  color: red;
}
```

##### Fixed

```scss
@mixin button {
  color: red;
}
```

##### Do

```scss
@mixin button {
  color: red;
}
```

### Differences from the source

Sass's at-rules are always known; the rule checks the CSS at-rules against the same table as `css/at-rule-no-unknown`.

## `scss/comment-no-loud` — Silent comments, not loud ones

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-scss` · `codelaw-rules-scss` · **Languages:** SCSS
- **Fix:** `suggest` (a `//` comment is not copied into the CSS; a comment meant for the output must stay `/* */`)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** no preset
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/scss/comment-no-loud.md

### What it checks

A comment in SCSS is written `//`, not `/* */` (which Sass copies into the CSS); `/*! … */` is kept.

**Why:** Notes for authors don't belong in the shipped stylesheet.

### How to fix

1. Write the comment with `//`.

### Examples

#### SCSS

##### Don't

```scss
/* note */
a {
  color: red;
}
```

##### Do

```scss
// note
a {
  color: red;
}
```

## `scss/declaration-nested-properties` — No nested properties

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-scss` · `codelaw-rules-scss` · **Languages:** SCSS
- **Fix:** `manual` (expanding nested properties rewrites a block into declarations, which the author should review)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** no preset
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/scss/declaration-nested-properties.md

### What it checks

Properties aren't nested under a shared prefix (`font: { family: x; }`): each is written out (`font-family: x`).

**Why:** A reader searches for `font-family`, not `family`.

### How to fix

1. Write each nested property as a full declaration.

### Examples

#### SCSS

##### Don't

```scss
a {
  font: {
    family: serif;
  }
}
```

##### Do

```scss
a {
  font-family: serif;
}
```

## `scss/declaration-nested-properties-no-divided-groups` — Nested properties of one prefix are in one group

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-scss` · `codelaw-rules-scss` · **Languages:** SCSS
- **Fix:** `manual` (merging the groups moves declarations, which can change which one wins)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:scss/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:scss/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/scss/declaration-nested-properties-no-divided-groups.md

### What it checks

A block doesn't hold two nested-property groups with the same prefix.

**Why:** The second group is easy to miss.

### How to fix

1. Merge the two groups.

### Examples

#### SCSS

##### Don't

```scss
a {
  font: {
    size: 1px;
  }
  color: red;
  font: {
    weight: bold;
  }
}
```

##### Do

```scss
a {
  font: {
    size: 1px;
    weight: bold;
  }
  color: red;
}
```

## `scss/dimension-no-non-numeric-values` — No dimension built from interpolated text

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-scss` · `codelaw-rules-scss` · **Languages:** SCSS
- **Fix:** `suggest` (multiplying needs the variable to hold a number; one that holds text would now fail to compile)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** no preset


##### Do

```scss
}
```

## `scss/dollar-variable-no-missing-interpolation` — Variables in at-rule names are interpolated

- **Fix:** `auto`

## `scss/dollar-variable-pattern` — `$variables` are kebab-case

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-scss` · `codelaw-rules-scss` · **Languages:** SCSS
- **Fix:** `manual` (renaming must update every use of the variable)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:scss/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/scss/dollar-variable-pattern.md

### What it checks

`$variable` names match a pattern, kebab-case by default.

**Why:** A consistent scheme makes names predictable across a codebase.

### Options

| Option | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `pattern` | `string` | `"^[a-z][a-z0-9]*(-[a-z0-9]+)*$"` | a regular expression the name, without its `$`, must match |

### How to fix

1. Rename the variable to match the pattern.
2. Rename every use of it.

### Examples

#### SCSS

##### Don't

```scss
$FontSize: 16px;
```

##### Do

```scss
$font-size: 16px;
```

### Differences from the source

The pattern applies to declarations, not to the names in an `@each` or a mixin's parameter list.

## `scss/function-color-channel` — Colour channels are read with `color.channel()`

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-scss` · `codelaw-rules-scss` · **Languages:** SCSS
- **Fix:** `suggest` (`color.channel()` returns the channel in the space named, which can differ in unit from the legacy function)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** no preset
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/scss/function-color-channel.md

### What it checks

`red($c)`, `hue($c)` and the other channel functions are written `color.channel($c, "red", $space: rgb)`.

**Why:** The legacy functions are deprecated in Dart Sass.

### How to fix

```scss
  width: red($c);
}
```

##### Do

```scss

  width: color.channel($c, "red", $space: rgb);
}
```

## `scss/function-color-relative` — No legacy relative colour functions

## `scss/function-disallowed-list` — No Sass function the project disallows

### What it checks

A function named in `list` isn't called. With no option set, the rule does nothing.

**Why:** A project steers its authors to its own helpers.

### Options

| Option | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `list` | `string[]` | `[]` | the function names disallowed (`/re/` for a regular expression) |

### How to fix

## `scss/function-no-unknown` — No unknown functions (SCSS)

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-scss` · `codelaw-rules-scss` · **Languages:** SCSS
- **Fix:** `suggest` (the known CSS and Sass functions within two edits are offered as choices, nearest first; a name with none near is manual)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:scss/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/scss/function-no-unknown.md

### What it checks

Every function called is a CSS function, a Sass built-in (global or `module.name`), or one the file defines with `@function`. A file that loads names it cannot see — `@import`, or `@use … as *` — is not checked.

**Why:** A browser drops a declaration whose value has an unknown function, and Sass passes the call through as plain CSS, so a typo fails silently.

### Options

| Option | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ignoreFunctions` | `string[]` | `[]` | functions to accept; `/regex/` for a pattern |

### How to fix

1. Correct the function name.
2. If it comes from a library, call it through its module (`lib.name()`), or add it to `ignoreFunctions`.

### Examples

#### SCSS

##### Don't

```scss
.a {
  width: percentag(0.5);
}
```

##### Fixed

```scss
.a {
  width: percentage(0.5);
}
```

##### Do

```scss
@use "sass:math";

.a {
  width: math.percentage(0.5);
}
```

### Differences from the source

Calls through a namespace (`ns.name()`) are not judged: the namespace's members are outside the file.

## `scss/load-no-partial-leading-underscore` — No leading underscore in a loaded partial

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-scss` · `codelaw-rules-scss` · **Languages:** SCSS
- **Fix:** `auto`
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:scss/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:scss/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/scss/load-no-partial-leading-underscore.md


### Differences from the source

Plain CSS imports (`.css`, URLs) and `sass:` modules are skipped.

## `scss/max-nesting-depth` — Limit nesting depth

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-scss` · `codelaw-rules-scss` · **Languages:** SCSS
- **Fix:** `suggest` (a too-deep rule whose parent holds nothing else is joined with it (`.d { .e {} }` becomes `.d .e {}`), compiling to the same CSS; the reviewer confirms the flatter source is wanted. Any other nesting is manual)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:scss/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/scss/max-nesting-depth.md

### What it checks

A style rule nests at most `max` levels inside other style rules (default 3): `.a { .b { .c { .d {} } } }` is three levels of nesting.

**Why:** Deep nesting couples a rule to the markup's shape, raises specificity, and produces long selectors nobody wrote on purpose.

### Options

| Option | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `max` | `number` | `3` | the deepest nesting allowed |

### How to fix

1. Lift the inner rule out and give it its own class.
2. Use `&-suffix` (BEM-style names) instead of a new level.

### Examples

#### SCSS

##### Don't

```scss
.a {
  .b {
    .c {
      .d {
        .e {
          color: red;
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

##### Fixed

```scss
.a {
  .b {
    .c {
      .d .e {
        color: red;
      }
    }
  }
}
```

##### Do

```scss
.a {
  .b {
    .c {
      .d {
        color: red;
      }
    }
  }
}
```

### Differences from the source

Nested properties (`font: { … }`) and at-rules such as `@media` and `@include` do not count as a level; only style rules do.

## `scss/no-duplicate-dollar-variables` — No duplicate `$variables`

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-scss` · `codelaw-rules-scss` · **Languages:** SCSS
- **Fix:** `auto` (auto when nothing between the two declarations reads the variable, so the earlier value is a dead store and goes; otherwise the earlier value is read and the fix is the author's)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:scss/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:scss/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/scss/no-duplicate-dollar-variables.md

### What it checks

A `$variable` is declared once per scope. A later `!default` declaration is not a duplicate, and a variable declared in another block is a different one.

**Why:** The second declaration silently replaces the first, so the first is dead code or a mistake.

### How to fix

1. Delete the declaration that should not win.
2. Rename one of them if both are meant.

### Examples

#### SCSS

##### Don't

```scss
$gap: 4px;
$gap: 8px;
```

##### Fixed

```scss
$gap: 8px;
```

##### Do

```scss
$gap: 4px;
$gap-large: 8px;
```

### Differences from the source

`ignoreDefaults` is always on: a `!default` redeclaration is accepted.

## `scss/no-duplicate-mixins` — No duplicate mixins

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-scss` · `codelaw-rules-scss` · **Languages:** SCSS
- **Fix:** `auto` (auto when no `@include` of the mixin stands between the two definitions, so nothing uses the earlier one and it goes; otherwise which definition each include meant is the author's call)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:scss/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:scss/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/scss/no-duplicate-mixins.md

### What it checks

A mixin is defined once per scope.

**Why:** The later definition replaces the earlier one; every `@include` before it silently gets the other body.

### How to fix

1. Delete or rename one of the definitions.

### Examples

#### SCSS

##### Don't

```scss
@mixin shadow {
  box-shadow: none;
}
@mixin shadow {
  box-shadow: 0 0 1px;
}
```

##### Fixed

```scss
@mixin shadow {
  box-shadow: 0 0 1px;
}
```

##### Do

```scss
@mixin shadow {
  box-shadow: none;
}
@mixin shadow-soft {
  box-shadow: 0 0 1px;
}
```

### Differences from the source

Two scopes may use the same name.

## `scss/no-global-function-names` — No global function names

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-scss` · `codelaw-rules-scss` · **Languages:** SCSS
- **Fix:** `auto`
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:scss/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/scss/no-global-function-names.md

### What it checks

The built-in functions Dart Sass moved into modules are called through their module: `map.get()`, not `map-get()`; `math.percentage()`, not `percentage()`. Functions that are also plain CSS (`min`, `max`, `round`, `abs`, `grayscale`, `invert`, `saturate`, `opacity`) are not reported: a call to one may be CSS.

**Why:** The global names are deprecated in Dart Sass and go away in 3.0. Module functions also keep a file's names from colliding.

### Examples

#### SCSS

##### Don't

```scss
.a {
  width: map-get($sizes, small);
}
```

##### Do

```scss
@use "sass:map";

.a {
  width: map.get($sizes, small);
}
```

### Differences from the source

stylelint-scss reports the global names it lists; this rule reports the module-moved built-ins and fixes the renames, adding each `@use "sass:…"` once. The colour adjusters are reported without a fix.

## `scss/no-import` — No `@import`

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-scss` · `codelaw-rules-scss` · **Languages:** SCSS
- **Fix:** `suggest` (`@use` namespaces what it loads and loads it once, so a bare swap can change what resolves)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:scss/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/scss/no-import.md

### What it checks

`@import` is not used for Sass files: Dart Sass deprecates it and removes it in 3.0. Load a file with `@use`, or re-export it with `@forward`. An import that stays a plain CSS `@import` (a `url()`, an `http://` address, a `.css` file, or one with a media query) is allowed.

**Why:** `@import` puts everything it loads in one global scope; two files can silently overwrite each other's variables and mixins, and a file imported twice is compiled twice.

### How to fix

1. Replace `@import "file"` with `@use "file"`; the members are then reached as `file.$name`, `file.mixin()`.
2. Use `@use "file" as *` to keep the old unprefixed names while migrating.
3. In an index file that only gathers other files, use `@forward`.

### Examples

#### SCSS

##### Don't

```scss
@import "variables";
@import "mixins";
```

##### Do

```scss
@use "variables";
@use "mixins";
```

### Differences from the source

Plain CSS imports are not reported. The fix is offered for a single quoted path; it is `suggest` because `@use` changes how the file's members are named.

## `scss/no-slash-division` — No `/` as division

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-scss` · `codelaw-rules-scss` · **Languages:** SCSS
- **Fix:** `suggest` (`math.div` needs a `@use` of sass:math, and a slash may be CSS)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:scss/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/scss/no-slash-division.md

### What it checks

Division is written `math.div($a, $b)`, not `$a / $b`. A `/` that Sass treats as a plain separator is left alone: `font: 12px/1.5`, `grid-area: 1 / 2`, and anything inside `calc()`.

**Why:** Dart Sass deprecates `/` as division and removes it in 3.0; the slash is ambiguous with CSS separators.

### How to fix

1. Add `@use "sass:math";` at the top of the file.
2. Replace `$a / $b` with `math.div($a, $b)`.

### Examples

#### SCSS

##### Don't

```scss
.a {
  width: $total / 3;
}
```

##### Do

```scss
@use "sass:math";

.a {
  width: math.div($total, 3);
}
```

### Differences from the source

The check is by operand: a `$variable`, or numbers inside a parenthesised expression. `font: 12px/1.5` is never reported.

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-scss` · `codelaw-rules-scss` · **Languages:** SCSS
- **Fix:** `manual` (whether the member is dead or should be used is the author's call)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** no preset
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/scss/no-unused-private-members.md

### What it checks

A private (`-` or `_`) variable, mixin, function or placeholder is used in the file that declares it.

**Why:** Nobody else can use it.

### How to fix

### Examples

#### SCSS

##### Don't

```scss

  color: red;
}
```

##### Do

```scss

  margin: $-gap;
}
```

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-scss` · `codelaw-rules-scss` · **Languages:** SCSS
- **Fix:** `manual` (where the import belongs is the author's call)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** no preset

## `scss/todo-marker` — SCSS TODO comments carry a ticket and, when asked, a date

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-scss` · `codelaw-rules-scss` · **Languages:** SCSS
- **Fix:** `manual` (a ticket and a date are facts about the work that only the author knows; the engine can't invent them)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:scss/markers` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/scss/todo-marker.md

### What it checks

A comment line that opens with a marker tag (`TODO`, `FIXME`, `HACK` by default) in a `//` or `/* … */` comment carries a ticket, and a date when the project asks for one: `TODO(ABC-123, 2027-01-31): text`. The ticket and the date go in the parentheses, in either order, either one optional unless required; any other item in them (an owner's name) is ignored. The tag must start the comment line, so a sentence that merely mentions a TODO is not a marker.

A date that is written is always enforced, whether or not `require_date` is set: it is **expired** from the as-of date on (`--as-of`, `CODELAW_AS_OF`, else `HEAD`'s commit date, never the clock: [SR-BASELINE](https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/records/0104_baseline-and-deprecations.md) decision 9) and is a **warning** for the `warn_days` before it. A date that is not a calendar day is reported too. With no as-of date, only the missing and the malformed are reported.

**Why:** A TODO with no ticket has no owner and no place to be tracked, and one with no date never comes due; both outlive the people who wrote them. Naming a ticket ties the comment to the work, and a date makes the comment fail loudly the day it is overdue instead of rotting quietly.

**Configuration** is the `[todo]` table of `codelaw.toml` ([SR-CONFIG](https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/records/0110_config.md) decision 11a), one for every language:

```toml
[todo]
tags           = ["TODO", "FIXME", "HACK"]   # the words that open a marker
require_ticket = true                         # a ticket is required (default)
require_date   = false                        # a date is required (default: only a written date is enforced)
ticket_pattern = "[A-Z][A-Z0-9]+-\\d+"        # a whole ticket must match this regular expression
warn_days      = 14                           # warn this many days before the date
```

**A repo full of bare TODOs** gets every one of them at once. Take them into the baseline (`codelaw baseline`) and pay them down, or set `require_ticket = false` and let the rule enforce only the dates that are written.

### How to fix

1. Open or find the ticket for the work and write it in the parentheses: `TODO(ABC-123): …`.
2. When the project asks for a date (`require_date`), or the work has a deadline, add it: `TODO(ABC-123, 2027-01-31): …`.
3. For an expired marker: do the work and delete the comment; or, if the work really moves, change the date and say why in the text.
4. If the comment is not a to-do, rewrite it so it does not open with the tag.

### Examples

#### SCSS

##### Don't

```scss
// TODO: replace with the spacing token
.card { padding: 12px; }
```

##### Do

```scss
// TODO(UI-40): replace with the spacing token
.card { padding: 12px; }
```

## `sec-html/angularjs-url-expression` — AngularJS URLs use ng-href and ng-src

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-security-html` · `codelaw-rules-security-html` · **Languages:** HTML
- **Fix:** `suggest` (the expression's value should be checked too; the rename is only the first step)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:sec-html/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-html/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/sec-html/angularjs-url-expression.md

### What it checks

In a page that uses AngularJS, `href="{{…}}"` and `src="{{…}}"` are written `ng-href` and `ng-src`.

**Why:** The browser requests the literal `{{…}}` before AngularJS fills it in, and an unvetted expression in a URL is an injection point; the `ng-` forms are set only after interpolation.

### Examples

#### HTML

##### Don't

```html
<div ng-app><a href="{{ profileUrl }}">Profile</a></div>
```

##### Do

```html
<div ng-app><a ng-href="{{ profileUrl }}">Profile</a></div>
```

## `sec-html/csp-meta-unsafe` — A meta Content Security Policy does not allow unsafe script

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-security-html` · `codelaw-rules-security-html` · **Languages:** HTML
- **Fix:** `suggest` (`'unsafe-inline'` is replaced with a `'sha256-…'` hash of each inline script, or dropped when there is none, when no element has an inline event handler; a script edited later then needs its hash again. `'unsafe-eval'`, `*` and `data:` are manual)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:sec-html/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-html/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/sec-html/csp-meta-unsafe.md

### What it checks

A `<meta http-equiv="Content-Security-Policy">` does not allow `'unsafe-inline'`, `'unsafe-eval'`, `*` or `data:` as a script source.

**Why:** Each of them lets injected script run, which is what the policy exists to stop.

### How to fix

1. Move inline script into files, or give it a nonce or a hash (`'nonce-…'`, `'sha256-…'`).
2. Remove `'unsafe-eval'` and replace `eval`, `new Function` and string timers.
3. List the origins scripts load from instead of `*` or `data:`.

### Examples

#### HTML

##### Don't

```html
<meta http-equiv="Content-Security-Policy" content="script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'">
```

##### Fixed

```html
<meta http-equiv="Content-Security-Policy" content="script-src 'self'">
```

##### Do

```html
<meta http-equiv="Content-Security-Policy" content="script-src 'self' 'nonce-r4nd0m'">
```

## `sec-html/form-csrf-token` — A POST form carries a CSRF token

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-security-html` · `codelaw-rules-security-html` · **Languages:** HTML
- **Fix:** `manual` (which token the server checks depends on its framework)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:sec-html/strict` at `warn`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/sec-html/form-csrf-token.md

### What it checks

A `<form method="post">` has a hidden anti-forgery field, or a template tag that writes one.

**Why:** Without a token another site can submit the form with the signed-in user's cookies.

### Options

| Option | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `names` | `string[]` | `[]` | extra names (field names or template tags) that count as a CSRF token, besides csrf, xsrf, authenticity_token, antiforgery, csrfmiddlewaretoken, __requestverificationtoken and _token |

### How to fix

1. Add the framework's field: `{% csrf_token %}` (Django), `@csrf` (Laravel), `<%= csrf_meta_tags %>` / `authenticity_token` (Rails), `{{ form.hidden_tag() }}` (Flask-WTF), or a hidden `_csrf` input.
2. If the form posts to another site, ignore it with `exceptions`.

### Examples

#### HTML

##### Don't

```html
<form method="post" action="/transfer"><input name="to"></form>
```

##### Do

```html
<form method="post" action="/transfer"><input type="hidden" name="csrf_token" value="{{ csrf_token }}"><input name="to"></form>
```

## `sec-html/iframe-allow-powerful` — A cross-origin iframe is not given a powerful feature

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-security-html` · `codelaw-rules-security-html` · **Languages:** HTML
- **Fix:** `suggest` (the powerful features are removed from `allow` (the attribute with them when nothing else is left); the framed page then can't use them, which the reviewer confirms)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:sec-html/strict` at `warn`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/sec-html/iframe-allow-powerful.md

### What it checks

An `<iframe>` whose `src` is on another origin does not list `camera`, `microphone`, `geolocation`, `payment` or another powerful feature in `allow`.

**Why:** The framed site gets the permission prompt, with the page's name on it, and whatever that site serves later inherits the grant.

### How to fix

1. Drop the feature from `allow`.
2. Or limit it to the origin that needs it: `allow="camera https://meet.example.com"`, and keep `'none'` for the rest.

### Examples

#### HTML

##### Don't

```html
<iframe src="https://meet.example.com/room" allow="camera; microphone"></iframe>
```

##### Fixed

```html
<iframe src="https://meet.example.com/room"></iframe>
```

##### Do

```html
<iframe src="https://meet.example.com/room" allow="fullscreen"></iframe>
```

## `sec-html/iframe-sandbox` — An iframe is sandboxed

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-security-html` · `codelaw-rules-security-html` · **Languages:** HTML
- **Fix:** `suggest` (the framed page may need `allow-*` tokens, which only its author knows)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:sec-html/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-html/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/sec-html/iframe-sandbox.md

### What it checks

An `<iframe>` has a `sandbox` attribute, and one that allows scripts does not also allow the same origin.

**Why:** A framed page without `sandbox` runs with every power a top-level page has; `allow-scripts` with `allow-same-origin` lets it remove its own sandbox.

### Examples

#### HTML

##### Don't

```html
<iframe src="/widget"></iframe>
```

##### Do

```html
<iframe sandbox src="/widget"></iframe>
```

## `sec-html/no-credentials-in-url` — No username and password in a URL

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-security-html` · `codelaw-rules-security-html` · **Languages:** HTML
- **Fix:** `suggest` (the `user:password@` part of the URL is removed; the link then asks for credentials instead of carrying them, which the reviewer confirms)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:sec-html/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-html/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/sec-html/no-credentials-in-url.md

### What it checks

A URL attribute does not carry `user:password@` in front of its host.

**Why:** A URL is stored in history, logs, referrers and bookmarks, so a credential written into one is disclosed to all of them.

### How to fix

1. Remove the credentials from the URL.
2. Send them in an `Authorization` header, or keep the request on the server.

### Examples

#### HTML

##### Don't

```html

```

##### Do

```html
<a href="https://intranet.example.com/">Admin</a>
```

## `sec-html/no-external-base` — <base> stays on this origin

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-security-html` · `codelaw-rules-security-html` · **Languages:** HTML
- **Fix:** `suggest` (the `<base>` goes and every relative URL of the page is written absolute against its `href`, so each still goes where it went; the reviewer confirms the other origin is meant. A page with a `srcset`, a template URL or a dot segment is manual)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:sec-html/strict` at `warn`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/sec-html/no-external-base.md

### What it checks

A `<base href>` is a path, not a URL on another origin.

**Why:** Every relative URL, form action and script on the page resolves against `<base>`, so one that points elsewhere hands them all to that site.

### How to fix

1. Delete the `<base>` and write the URLs you need in full.
2. Or make its `href` a path on this origin, such as `/app/`.

### Examples

#### HTML

##### Don't

```html
<base href="https://cdn.example.com/app/">
<link rel="stylesheet" href="app.css">
```

##### Fixed

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.example.com/app/app.css">
```

##### Do

```html
<base href="/app/">
```

## `sec-html/no-inline-event-handler` — No inline event handlers

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-security-html` · `codelaw-rules-security-html` · **Languages:** HTML
- **Fix:** `manual` (the handler's code has to move into a script that attaches it)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:sec-html/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-html/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/sec-html/no-inline-event-handler.md

### What it checks

No element has an inline event handler (`onclick`, `onerror`, `onload`, …).

**Why:** An inline handler runs script from an attribute, so a strict Content Security Policy that blocks inline script blocks it too, and a value interpolated into it becomes cross-site scripting.

### How to fix

1. Give the element an id or a class.
2. Attach the listener with `addEventListener` in a script file.
3. Delete the `on…` attribute.

### Examples

#### HTML

##### Don't

```html
<button type="button" onclick="save()">Save</button>
```

##### Do

```html
<button type="button" id="save">Save</button>
```

## `sec-html/no-javascript-url` — No javascript: URLs

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-security-html` · `codelaw-rules-security-html` · **Languages:** HTML
- **Fix:** `suggest` (an `<a href="javascript:void(0)">` runs nothing and becomes `<button type="button">`, its other attributes kept; it then looks like a button until styled. A `javascript:` URL that runs script is manual)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:sec-html/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-html/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/sec-html/no-javascript-url.md

### What it checks

An `href`, `src`, `action`, `formaction`, `xlink:href` or `<object data>` is never a `javascript:` URL.

**Why:** A `javascript:` URL runs script from an attribute, so it is cross-site scripting waiting for one interpolated value, and a strict Content Security Policy blocks it.

### How to fix

1. Replace a `javascript:` link with a `<button type="button">` and attach the listener with `addEventListener`.
2. Point `href`, `src`, `action` or `formaction` at a real URL.

### Examples

#### HTML

##### Don't

```html
<a href="javascript:void(0)">Menu</a>
```

##### Fixed

```html
<button type="button">Menu</button>
```

##### Do

```html
<button type="button" id="menu">Menu</button>
```

## `sec-html/no-mixed-content` — Subresources and forms load over HTTPS

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-security-html` · `codelaw-rules-security-html` · **Languages:** HTML
- **Fix:** `suggest` (the host may not serve HTTPS; check that it does before switching)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:sec-html/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-html/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/sec-html/no-mixed-content.md

### What it checks

A `src`, a form `action`, a stylesheet or script `href` and a download link never use `http://`.

**Why:** A resource fetched over plain HTTP can be read and changed by anyone on the network, and a browser blocks or warns about it on an HTTPS page.

### Examples

#### HTML

##### Don't

```html
<script src="http://cdn.example.com/lib.js"></script>
```

##### Do

```html
<script src="https://cdn.example.com/lib.js"></script>
```

## `sec-html/no-plugin-embed` — No <object>, <embed> or <applet>

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-security-html` · `codelaw-rules-security-html` · **Languages:** HTML
- **Fix:** `suggest` (an `<embed>` of a picture, a video or a sound, by its `type` or file extension, becomes `<img>`, `<video controls>` or `<audio controls>`; anything else (Flash, a document) is manual)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:sec-html/strict` at `warn`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/sec-html/no-plugin-embed.md

### What it checks

The page does not use `<object>`, `<embed>` or `<applet>` (an `<object>` that holds an image is fine).

**Why:** They load a plugin or another document with the page's trust, and the plugins that needed them are gone from browsers.

### How to fix

1. Use `<img>`, `<video>` or `<audio>` for media.
2. Use a sandboxed `<iframe>` for another document.
3. Use `<a download>` for a file to fetch.

### Examples

#### HTML

##### Don't

```html
<embed src="movie.mp4">
```

##### Do

```html
<video src="movie.mp4" controls></video>
```

## `sec-html/no-secret-in-hidden-input` — No secret in a hidden input

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-security-html` · `codelaw-rules-security-html` · **Languages:** HTML
- **Fix:** `manual` (where the secret should live is a design decision)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:sec-html/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-html/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/sec-html/no-secret-in-hidden-input.md

### What it checks

A hidden input named like a password, token, secret or API key does not hold a literal value (CSRF tokens are excluded).

**Why:** A hidden field is part of the page everyone receives, so a secret written into it is disclosed to every visitor.

### How to fix

1. Keep the secret on the server and send a session or a reference instead.
2. If the field is an anti-forgery token, name it `csrf_token`, `_csrf` or the framework's own name.

### Examples

#### HTML

##### Don't

```html
<input type="hidden" name="api_key" value="sk_live_51Habc">
```

##### Do

```html
<input type="hidden" name="csrf_token" value="{{ csrf_token }}">
```

## `sec-html/no-sensitive-comments` — No comment that exposes a secret or an internal host

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-security-html` · `codelaw-rules-security-html` · **Languages:** HTML
- **Fix:** `auto`
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:sec-html/strict` at `warn`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/sec-html/no-sensitive-comments.md

### What it checks

An HTML comment does not hold a password, key, token, private IP address, internal host name, or a note to remove it before release.

**Why:** Comments are sent to every visitor, so a developer's note becomes a disclosure.

### Examples

#### HTML

##### Don't

```html
<!-- password: hunter2 -->
<p>Welcome</p>
```

##### Do

```html
<p>Welcome</p>
```

## `sec-html/no-srcdoc-script` — An iframe's srcdoc holds no script

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-security-html` · `codelaw-rules-security-html` · **Languages:** HTML
- **Fix:** `suggest` (the choices are an empty `sandbox` (the default), or `sandbox="allow-scripts"` when the framed document must run; either gives it an opaque origin, and `allow-same-origin` is never offered)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:sec-html/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-html/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/sec-html/no-srcdoc-script.md

### What it checks

An `<iframe srcdoc>` does not contain a `<script>`, an event handler or a `javascript:` URL.

**Why:** `srcdoc` content runs with the origin of the page that holds it unless the iframe is sandboxed, so script in it is script in the page.

### How to fix

1. Move the document to its own file and load it with `src`.
2. Add `sandbox` without `allow-same-origin`.

### Examples

#### HTML

##### Don't

```html
<iframe srcdoc="&lt;script&gt;track()&lt;/script&gt;"></iframe>
```

##### Fixed (sandbox)

```html
<iframe sandbox srcdoc="&lt;script&gt;track()&lt;/script&gt;"></iframe>
```

##### Fixed (sandbox, scripts allowed)

```html
<iframe sandbox="allow-scripts" srcdoc="&lt;script&gt;track()&lt;/script&gt;"></iframe>
```

##### Do

```html
<iframe sandbox src="/track.html"></iframe>
```

## `sec-html/no-template-html-sink` — No template binding that writes HTML

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-security-html` · `codelaw-rules-security-html` · **Languages:** HTML
- **Fix:** `suggest` (the HTML binding becomes its text binding (`[innerHTML]` to `[textContent]`, `v-html` to `v-text`, `x-html` to `x-text`), so the value shows as text; markup it was meant to carry then shows escaped. `[outerHTML]` has no text twin and is manual)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:sec-html/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-html/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/sec-html/no-template-html-sink.md

### What it checks

A template does not bind a value as HTML: Angular `[innerHTML]` and `[outerHTML]`, Vue `v-html`, Alpine `x-html`.

**Why:** The value is written into the page as markup, so any part of it a user controls is cross-site scripting.

### How to fix

1. Bind text instead (`{{ value }}`, `v-text`, `x-text`, `[textContent]`).
2. If it must be HTML, sanitise it with a maintained library such as DOMPurify and bind the sanitised result.

### Examples

#### HTML

##### Don't

```html
<div [innerHTML]="comment"></div>
```

##### Fixed

```html
<div [textContent]="comment"></div>
```

##### Do

```html
<div>{{ comment }}</div>
```

## `sec-html/no-unsafe-template-interpolation` — No template syntax that turns escaping off

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-security-html` · `codelaw-rules-security-html` · **Languages:** HTML
- **Fix:** `suggest` (`{{{ x }}}` becomes `{{ x }}`, `|safe` goes and `<%- x %>` becomes `<%= x %>`, so the template escapes the value; markup the value was meant to carry then shows as text, which the reviewer confirms. `autoescape off` is manual)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:sec-html/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-html/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/sec-html/no-unsafe-template-interpolation.md

### What it checks

A template does not turn escaping off: Handlebars `{{{ }}}`, Jinja and Nunjucks `|safe`, Django `{% autoescape off %}`, EJS `<%-`.

**Why:** The value is written into the page as markup, so any part of it a user controls is cross-site scripting.

### How to fix

1. Use the escaping form: `{{ value }}` (Handlebars, Jinja, Django), `<%= value %>` (EJS).
2. If the value must be markup, sanitise it with a maintained library first and mark only the sanitised result safe.

### Examples

#### HTML

##### Don't

```html
<p>{{{ comment }}}</p>
```

##### Do

```html
<p>{{ comment }}</p>
```

## `sec-html/password-form-post` — A form with a password sends it with POST over HTTPS

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-security-html` · `codelaw-rules-security-html` · **Languages:** HTML
- **Fix:** `suggest` (a server that reads only the query string has to change with the form)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:sec-html/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-html/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/sec-html/password-form-post.md

### What it checks

A form holding a password field sets `method="post"` and does not post to an `http:` URL.

**Why:** A form with no `method` or with `method="get"` puts the password in the URL, where history, logs and referrers keep it; an `http:` action sends it in the clear.

### Examples

#### HTML

##### Don't

```html
<form action="/login" method="get"><input type="password" name="pw"></form>
```

##### Do

```html
<form action="/login" method="post"><input type="password" name="pw"></form>
```

## `sec-html/referrer-policy` — No referrer policy that leaks full URLs

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-security-html` · `codelaw-rules-security-html` · **Languages:** HTML
- **Fix:** `suggest` (a partner may rely on the full referrer; the safer value is a suggestion)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:sec-html/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-html/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/sec-html/referrer-policy.md

### What it checks

A `referrerpolicy` attribute or `<meta name="referrer">` is not `unsafe-url` or `no-referrer-when-downgrade`.

**Why:** Both send the full URL of the page, query string included, to other sites, and a URL often holds a token or an identifier.

### Examples

#### HTML

##### Don't

```html
<a href="https://other.example/" referrerpolicy="unsafe-url">Other</a>
```

##### Do

```html
<a href="https://other.example/" referrerpolicy="strict-origin-when-cross-origin">Other</a>
```

## `sec-html/sri-crossorigin` — A script or stylesheet with an integrity hash has crossorigin

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-security-html` · `codelaw-rules-security-html` · **Languages:** HTML
- **Fix:** `suggest` (`anonymous` is right unless the file needs credentials; the suggestion assumes it does not)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:sec-html/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-html/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/sec-html/sri-crossorigin.md

### What it checks

A `<script>` or `<link>` from another origin that has `integrity` also has `crossorigin`.

**Why:** Without `crossorigin` the browser fetches the file without CORS and cannot read it to check the hash, so the `integrity` protects nothing.

### Examples

#### HTML

##### Don't

```html
<script src="https://cdn.example.com/lib.js" integrity="sha384-oqVuAfXRKap7fdgcCY5uykM6+R9GqQ8K/uxy9rx7HNQlGYl1kPzQho1wx4JwY8wC"></script>
```

##### Do

```html
<script src="https://cdn.example.com/lib.js" integrity="sha384-oqVuAfXRKap7fdgcCY5uykM6+R9GqQ8K/uxy9rx7HNQlGYl1kPzQho1wx4JwY8wC" crossorigin="anonymous"></script>
```

## `sec-js/angularjs-sce-disabled` — No AngularJS strict contextual escaping switched off

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-security-js` · `codelaw-rules-security-js` · **Languages:** JavaScript, JSX, TypeScript, TSX
- **Fix:** `suggest` (switching `$sce` back on and narrowing the whitelist to `self` is fail-closed, but the reviewer adds the hosts the templates load from)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:sec-js/strict` at `warn` · `codelaw:sec-ts/strict` at `warn`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/sec-js/angularjs-sce-disabled.md

### What it checks

AngularJS's `$sce` stays on, `resourceUrlWhitelist` has no `"**"`, the href and image whitelists are not match-everything, and `$sce.trustAs*` is not given an unsanitized value.

**Your sanitizer:** a value passes when it is a call to one of the `sanitizers`: the built-in list (DOMPurify, sanitize-html, xss, escape-html, lodash and he `escape`, Trusted Types `createHTML`) plus your own, each matched by name and by the module it is imported from, so a local `function sanitize(x) { return x }` does not pass. `sanitizers_mode = "replace"` makes yours the only ones that count. It does not follow a value through a variable: `const c = clean(x)` then `c` at the sink is not a call. Add a project function with `sanitizers = [{ name = "sanitizeHtml", module = "@acme/security" }]`.

**Why:** `$sce` is what stops a bound string from becoming HTML, a script or a frame source; switching it off or trusting every value turns each binding into an XSS sink (CWE-79).

### Options

| Option | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sanitizers` | `call[]` | 10 entries (below) | functions whose result may reach the sink: a callee path (global) or { name, module }; `sanitizers_mode: replace` makes them the only ones that count |
| `sanitizers_mode` | `string` | `"extend"` | `extend` adds your `sanitizers` to the default list; `replace` uses only yours |

### How to fix

1. Leave `$sceProvider.enabled` at its default (`true`).
2. List the hosts a template may load from in `resourceUrlWhitelist`: `["self", "https://cdn.example.com/**"]`, not `"**"`.
3. Pass a value to `$sce.trustAsHtml` only after a sanitizer (`$sanitize`, DOMPurify) has cleaned it.

### Examples

#### JavaScript

##### Don't

```js
app.config(function ($sceProvider) {
  $sceProvider.enabled(false);
});
```

##### Do

```js
app.config(function ($sceProvider) {
  $sceProvider.enabled(true);
});
```

#### JSX

##### Don't

```jsx
app.config(function ($sceProvider) {
  $sceProvider.enabled(false);
});
```

##### Do

```jsx
app.config(function ($sceProvider) {
  $sceProvider.enabled(true);
});
```

#### TypeScript

##### Don't

```ts
app.config(function ($sceProvider) {
  $sceProvider.enabled(false);
});
```

##### Do

```ts
app.config(function ($sceProvider) {
  $sceProvider.enabled(true);
});
```

#### TSX

##### Don't

```tsx
app.config(function ($sceProvider) {
  $sceProvider.enabled(false);
});
```

##### Do

```tsx
app.config(function ($sceProvider) {
  $sceProvider.enabled(true);
});
```

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-security-js` · `codelaw-rules-security-js` · **Languages:** JavaScript, JSX, TypeScript, TSX

```js
res.cookie("sid", sid, { httpOnly: true, secure: true, sameSite: "lax" });
```

```js
res.cookie("sid", sid, { httpOnly: true, secure: true, sameSite: "lax" });
```

## `sec-js/express-session-secret` — express-session has a secret from the environment and a secure cookie

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-security-js` · `codelaw-rules-security-js` · **Languages:** JavaScript, JSX, TypeScript, TSX
- **Fix:** `manual` (where the secret comes from is a deployment decision)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:sec-js/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-js/strict` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-ts/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-ts/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/sec-js/express-session-secret.md

### What it checks

`express-session`, `cookie-session` and `session()` are not given a literal `secret`, and their cookie does not set `secure: false`.

**Why:** A secret in the source is in every clone and every build; anyone who has it forges a session cookie, and `secure: false` lets the cookie travel over plain HTTP (CWE-798, CWE-614).

### How to fix

1. Read the secret from the environment or a secret store, and rotate it if it was ever committed.
2. Set `cookie: { secure: true, httpOnly: true, sameSite: "lax" }` in production (behind a proxy, set `trust proxy`).

### Examples

#### JavaScript

##### Don't

```js
app.use(session({ secret: "keyboard cat", resave: false }));
```

##### Do

```js
app.use(session({ secret: process.env.SESSION_SECRET, resave: false }));
```

#### JSX

##### Don't

```jsx
app.use(session({ secret: "keyboard cat", resave: false }));
```

##### Do

```jsx
app.use(session({ secret: process.env.SESSION_SECRET, resave: false }));
```

#### TypeScript

##### Don't

```ts
app.use(session({ secret: "keyboard cat", resave: false }));
```

##### Do

```ts
app.use(session({ secret: process.env.SESSION_SECRET, resave: false }));
```

#### TSX

##### Don't

```tsx
app.use(session({ secret: "keyboard cat", resave: false }));
```

##### Do

```tsx
app.use(session({ secret: process.env.SESSION_SECRET, resave: false }));
```

## `sec-js/graphql-hardening` — A GraphQL server limits query depth and cost, and hides introspection

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-security-js` · `codelaw-rules-security-js` · **Languages:** JavaScript, JSX, TypeScript, TSX
- **Fix:** `manual` (the limits that fit the schema are a decision for the author)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:sec-js/strict` at `warn` · `codelaw:sec-ts/strict` at `warn`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/sec-js/graphql-hardening.md

### What it checks

An Apollo, Yoga or express-graphql server names a depth or cost limit in its options, and does not set `introspection: true`.

**Why:** A query can nest or fan out without bound and exhaust the server, and introspection hands an attacker the whole schema (CWE-770, CWE-200).

### How to fix

1. Add a depth limit (`graphql-depth-limit`) and a cost or complexity limit to `validationRules`, and cap the page size of list fields.
2. Turn introspection off in production, and use persisted queries where the clients are your own.

### Examples

#### JavaScript

##### Don't

```js
const server = new ApolloServer({ typeDefs, resolvers });
```

##### Do

```js
const server = new ApolloServer({
  typeDefs,
  resolvers,
  validationRules: [depthLimit(8)],
  introspection: process.env.NODE_ENV !== "production",
});
```

#### JSX

##### Don't

```jsx
const server = new ApolloServer({ typeDefs, resolvers });
```

##### Do

```jsx
const server = new ApolloServer({
  typeDefs,
  resolvers,
  validationRules: [depthLimit(8)],
  introspection: process.env.NODE_ENV !== "production",
});
```

#### TypeScript

##### Don't

```ts
const server = new ApolloServer({ typeDefs, resolvers });
```

##### Do

```ts
const server = new ApolloServer({
  typeDefs,
  resolvers,
  validationRules: [depthLimit(8)],
  introspection: process.env.NODE_ENV !== "production",
});
```

#### TSX

##### Don't

```tsx
const server = new ApolloServer({ typeDefs, resolvers });
```

##### Do

```tsx
const server = new ApolloServer({
  typeDefs,
  resolvers,
  validationRules: [depthLimit(8)],
  introspection: process.env.NODE_ENV !== "production",
});
```

## `sec-js/helmet-config` — helmet is not given false for a header it sets

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-security-js` · `codelaw-rules-security-js` · **Languages:** JavaScript, JSX, TypeScript, TSX
- **Fix:** `suggest` (deleting the `false` pair makes helmet fall back to its default for that header, which the reviewer checks against the app's inline scripts)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:sec-js/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-js/strict` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-ts/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-ts/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/sec-js/helmet-config.md

### What it checks

`helmet({ … })` does not set `contentSecurityPolicy`, `frameguard`, `hsts`, `noSniff`, `xssFilter` or the cross-origin policies to `false`.

**Why:** Each of these headers closes one class of attack (injected scripts, clickjacking, downgrade to HTTP, MIME sniffing); turning one off opens it again (CWE-693).

### How to fix

1. Keep the header on and tune it: give `contentSecurityPolicy` the directives the app needs.
2. If a header must go for one route, set it off for that route only, with a comment that says why.

### Examples

#### JavaScript

##### Don't

```js
app.use(helmet({ contentSecurityPolicy: false }));
```

##### Fixed

```js
app.use(helmet({  }));
```

##### Do

```js
app.use(helmet({ contentSecurityPolicy: { directives: { defaultSrc: ["'self'"] } } }));
```

#### JSX

##### Don't

```jsx
app.use(helmet({ contentSecurityPolicy: false }));
```

##### Fixed

```jsx
app.use(helmet({  }));
```

##### Do

```jsx
app.use(helmet({ contentSecurityPolicy: { directives: { defaultSrc: ["'self'"] } } }));
```

#### TypeScript

##### Don't

```ts
app.use(helmet({ contentSecurityPolicy: false }));
```

##### Fixed

```ts
app.use(helmet({  }));
```

##### Do

```ts
app.use(helmet({ contentSecurityPolicy: { directives: { defaultSrc: ["'self'"] } } }));
```

#### TSX

##### Don't

```tsx

```

##### Fixed

```tsx
app.use(helmet({  }));
```

##### Do

```tsx
app.use(helmet({ contentSecurityPolicy: { directives: { defaultSrc: ["'self'"] } } }));
```

## `sec-js/jwt-verify` — A JWT is verified with a named algorithm, never `none`

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-security-js` · `codelaw-rules-security-js` · **Languages:** JavaScript, JSX, TypeScript, TSX
- **Fix:** `suggest` (naming the algorithm is fail-closed, but the reviewer confirms it is the one the issuer signs with (RS256, HS256 or ES256))
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:sec-js/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-js/strict` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-ts/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-ts/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/sec-js/jwt-verify.md

### What it checks

`jwt.verify` is given an `algorithms` list, no algorithm is `none`, and `jwt.decode` is not the whole check.

**Why:** Without `algorithms` a token can pick its own: `none` carries no signature, and an RSA public key used as an HMAC secret lets anyone mint tokens (CWE-347). `decode` reads a token without checking it.

### How to fix

1. Pass `{ algorithms: ["RS256"] }` (or the one algorithm you issue with) to `jwt.verify`.
2. Never put `none` in the list, and never use a public key as an HMAC secret.
3. Use `jwt.decode` only to read a token that `jwt.verify` has already accepted.

### Examples

#### JavaScript

##### Don't

```js
const claims = jwt.verify(token, publicKey);
```

##### Fixed (RS256)

```js
const claims = jwt.verify(token, publicKey, { algorithms: ["RS256"] });
```

##### Fixed (HS256)

```js
const claims = jwt.verify(token, publicKey, { algorithms: ["HS256"] });
```

##### Fixed (ES256)

```js
const claims = jwt.verify(token, publicKey, { algorithms: ["ES256"] });
```

##### Do

```js
const claims = jwt.verify(token, publicKey, { algorithms: ["RS256"] });
```

#### JSX

##### Don't

```jsx
const claims = jwt.verify(token, publicKey);
```

##### Fixed (RS256)

```jsx
const claims = jwt.verify(token, publicKey, { algorithms: ["RS256"] });
```

##### Fixed (HS256)

```jsx
const claims = jwt.verify(token, publicKey, { algorithms: ["HS256"] });
```

##### Fixed (ES256)

```jsx
const claims = jwt.verify(token, publicKey, { algorithms: ["ES256"] });
```

##### Do

```jsx
const claims = jwt.verify(token, publicKey, { algorithms: ["RS256"] });
```

#### TypeScript

##### Don't

```ts
const claims = jwt.verify(token, publicKey);
```

##### Fixed (RS256)

```ts
const claims = jwt.verify(token, publicKey, { algorithms: ["RS256"] });
```

##### Fixed (HS256)

```ts

```

##### Fixed (ES256)

```ts

```

##### Do

```ts

```

#### TSX

##### Don't

```tsx

```

```tsx

```

##### Fixed (HS256)

```tsx

```

##### Fixed (ES256)

```tsx

```

##### Do


## `sec-js/missing-rate-limit` — A login or reset route has a rate limit

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-security-js` · `codelaw-rules-security-js` · **Languages:** JavaScript, JSX, TypeScript, TSX
- **Fix:** `manual` (the limits that fit the route are a decision for the author)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:sec-js/strict` at `warn` · `codelaw:sec-ts/strict` at `warn`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/sec-js/missing-rate-limit.md

### What it checks

A route that signs in, resets a password or checks a one-time code is registered with middleware, and the file mentions a rate limiter.

**Why:** Without a limit an attacker tries passwords, codes and reset tokens as fast as the server answers (CWE-307, CWE-770).

### How to fix

1. Add `express-rate-limit` (or the framework's equivalent) to the route: a few attempts per minute per address and per account.
2. Add a lock-out or a growing delay after repeated failures, and log them.

### Examples

#### JavaScript

##### Don't

```js
app.post("/login", (req, res) => {
  signIn(req, res);
});
```

##### Do

```js
const loginLimiter = rateLimit({ windowMs: 60000, max: 10 });
app.post("/login", loginLimiter, (req, res) => {
  signIn(req, res);
});
```

#### JSX

##### Don't

```jsx
app.post("/login", (req, res) => {
  signIn(req, res);
});
```

##### Do

```jsx
const loginLimiter = rateLimit({ windowMs: 60000, max: 10 });
app.post("/login", loginLimiter, (req, res) => {
  signIn(req, res);
});
```

#### TypeScript

##### Don't

```ts
app.post("/login", (req, res) => {
  signIn(req, res);
});
```

##### Do

```ts
const loginLimiter = rateLimit({ windowMs: 60000, max: 10 });
app.post("/login", loginLimiter, (req, res) => {
  signIn(req, res);
});
```

#### TSX

##### Don't

```tsx
app.post("/login", (req, res) => {
  signIn(req, res);
});
```

##### Do

```tsx
const loginLimiter = rateLimit({ windowMs: 60000, max: 10 });
app.post("/login", loginLimiter, (req, res) => {
  signIn(req, res);
});
```

## `sec-js/no-archive-slip` — No archive entry name written to disk unchecked

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-security-js` · `codelaw-rules-security-js` · **Languages:** JavaScript, JSX, TypeScript, TSX
- **Fix:** `manual` (what to do with an entry that leaves the folder (skip, stop, report) is a decision for the author)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:sec-js/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-js/strict` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-ts/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-ts/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/sec-js/no-archive-slip.md

### What it checks

A file written while unpacking an archive is not named by the entry's own path or name without a check that it stays inside the target folder.

**Why:** An entry named `../../etc/cron.d/x` or an absolute path writes outside the folder the code meant: the zip-slip bug (CWE-22).

### How to fix

1. Resolve the entry's path against the target folder and reject the entry when the result does not start with `target + path.sep`.
2. Skip symbolic links and absolute entry names; set a limit on the number and total size of entries (a zip bomb).

### Examples

#### JavaScript

##### Don't

```js
entry.pipe(fs.createWriteStream(path.join(dest, entry.path)));
```

##### Do

```js
const target = path.resolve(dest, entry.path);
if (!target.startsWith(dest + path.sep)) {
  throw new Error("archive entry leaves the folder");
}
entry.pipe(fs.createWriteStream(target));
```

#### JSX

##### Don't

```jsx
entry.pipe(fs.createWriteStream(path.join(dest, entry.path)));
```

##### Do

```jsx
const target = path.resolve(dest, entry.path);
if (!target.startsWith(dest + path.sep)) {
  throw new Error("archive entry leaves the folder");
}
entry.pipe(fs.createWriteStream(target));
```

#### TypeScript

##### Don't

```ts
entry.pipe(fs.createWriteStream(path.join(dest, entry.path)));
```

##### Do

```ts
const target = path.resolve(dest, entry.path);
if (!target.startsWith(dest + path.sep)) {
  throw new Error("archive entry leaves the folder");
}
entry.pipe(fs.createWriteStream(target));
```

#### TSX

##### Don't

```tsx
entry.pipe(fs.createWriteStream(path.join(dest, entry.path)));
```

##### Do

```tsx
const target = path.resolve(dest, entry.path);
if (!target.startsWith(dest + path.sep)) {
  throw new Error("archive entry leaves the folder");
}
entry.pipe(fs.createWriteStream(target));
```

## `sec-js/no-bad-tag-filter` — No regular expression that filters HTML tags

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-security-js` · `codelaw-rules-security-js` · **Languages:** JavaScript, JSX, TypeScript, TSX
- **Fix:** `suggest` (escaping shows the markup as text and a sanitizer keeps safe markup (the reviewer imports it); which one the page needs is the author's choice)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:sec-js/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-js/strict` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-ts/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-ts/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/sec-js/no-bad-tag-filter.md

### What it checks

A regular expression is not used to strip or test HTML tags (`/<script>/`, `/<[^>]*>/`); a sanitizer is.

**Why:** HTML is not regular: `<script >`, `<SCRIPT>`, `<scr<script>ipt>` and a tag split across lines slip past a pattern, and what is left still runs (CWE-116, CWE-185).

### How to fix

1. Sanitize with a library built for it: `DOMPurify.sanitize(html)` in the browser, `sanitize-html` on the server.
2. To show markup as text, escape it (`&lt;`) instead of removing it, or write it with `textContent`.

### Examples

#### JavaScript

##### Don't

```js
const clean = input.replace(/<script>/gi, "");
```

##### Fixed (escape)

```js
const clean = input.replace(/[&<>]/g, (c) => ({ "&": "&amp;", "<": "&lt;", ">": "&gt;" })[c]);
```

##### Fixed (sanitizer)

```js
const clean = DOMPurify.sanitize(input);
```

##### Do

```js
const clean = DOMPurify.sanitize(input);
```

#### JSX

##### Don't

```jsx
const clean = input.replace(/<script>/gi, "");
```

##### Fixed (escape)

```jsx
const clean = input.replace(/[&<>]/g, (c) => ({ "&": "&amp;", "<": "&lt;", ">": "&gt;" })[c]);
```

##### Fixed (sanitizer)

```jsx
const clean = DOMPurify.sanitize(input);
```

##### Do

```jsx
const clean = DOMPurify.sanitize(input);
```

#### TypeScript

##### Don't

```ts
const clean = input.replace(/<script>/gi, "");
```

##### Fixed (escape)

```ts
const clean = input.replace(/[&<>]/g, (c) => ({ "&": "&amp;", "<": "&lt;", ">": "&gt;" })[c]);
```

##### Fixed (sanitizer)

```ts

```

##### Do

```ts

```

#### TSX

##### Don't

```tsx

```

##### Fixed (escape)

## `sec-js/no-biased-random` — No byte taken modulo a number that does not divide 256

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-security-js` · `codelaw-rules-security-js` · **Languages:** JavaScript, JSX, TypeScript, TSX
- **Fix:** `suggest` (`crypto.randomInt` needs Node 14.10 or later, and a range that starts above zero needs the bounds written)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:sec-js/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-js/strict` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-ts/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-ts/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/sec-js/no-biased-random.md

### What it checks

A random byte or integer from `crypto.randomBytes` is not reduced with `%`; `crypto.randomInt(max)` does it without bias.

**Why:** `byte % 6` makes some results more likely than others (256 is not a multiple of 6), which weakens a token, a die or a shuffle (CWE-327).

### How to fix

### Examples

```js
const roll = crypto.randomBytes(1)[0] % 6;
```

##### Do

```js
const roll = crypto.randomInt(6);
```

##### Fixed

```js
const roll = crypto.randomInt(6);
```

#### JSX

##### Don't

```jsx
const roll = crypto.randomBytes(1)[0] % 6;
```

##### Do

```jsx

```

##### Fixed

```jsx
const roll = crypto.randomInt(6);
```

#### TypeScript

##### Don't

```ts

```

##### Do

```ts

```

##### Fixed

```ts

```

#### TSX

##### Don't

```tsx

```

##### Do

```tsx

```

##### Fixed

```tsx

```

## `sec-js/no-bidi-characters` — No hidden bidirectional control characters in code

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-security-js` · `codelaw-rules-security-js` · **Languages:** JavaScript, JSX, TypeScript, TSX
- **Fix:** `suggest` (a comment is removed whole, since its hidden text cannot be told from the rest; a string or regular expression with such a character has no mechanical fix)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:sec-js/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-js/strict` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-ts/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-ts/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/sec-js/no-bidi-characters.md

### What it checks

Source code, comments, strings and regular expressions hold no bidirectional control characters (U+202A–U+202E, U+2066–U+2069).

**Why:** These characters reorder how an editor and a review tool show the code, so what a reviewer reads is not what the compiler runs: the Trojan Source attack (CVE-2021-42574).

### How to fix

1. Delete the character: show hidden characters in the editor (or run `git diff --word-diff-regex=.`) and remove each one.
2. If a string needs right-to-left text, write the characters as escapes (`\u202E`) so the source does not hide them.

### Examples

#### JavaScript

##### Don't

```js
const level = readLevel();
// check the access level ‮ ⁦ admin
```

##### Do

```js
const level = readLevel();
```

##### Fixed

```js
const level = readLevel();
```

#### JSX

##### Don't

```jsx
const level = readLevel();
// check the access level ‮ ⁦ admin
```

##### Do

```jsx
const level = readLevel();
```

##### Fixed

```jsx
const level = readLevel();
```

#### TypeScript

##### Don't

```ts

// check the access level ‮ ⁦ admin
```

##### Do

```ts

```

##### Fixed

```ts

```

#### TSX

##### Don't

```tsx

```

##### Do

```tsx

```

##### Fixed


## `sec-js/no-child-process-shell` — No shell command built from a value

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-security-js` · `codelaw-rules-security-js` · **Languages:** JavaScript, JSX, TypeScript, TSX
- **Fix:** `manual` (the program and its arguments have to be separated by hand)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:sec-js/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-js/strict` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-ts/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-ts/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/sec-js/no-child-process-shell.md

### What it checks

`exec` and `execSync` (from `child_process`) are called with a literal command only, and `spawn`-style calls do not set `shell: true`.

**Why:** A command string is parsed by a shell, so a value spliced into it can add commands with `;`, `&&` or `$(…)` (CWE-78).

### How to fix

1. Call `execFile` or `spawn` with the program name first and the values as an array: no shell parses them.
2. Leave `shell` at its default (`false`); if a shell feature (a pipe, a glob) is needed, do it in the program, not in a command string.
3. A value that must reach a command is checked against an allow-list first.

### Examples

#### JavaScript

##### Don't

```js
const { exec } = require("child_process");
exec("convert " + name + " out.png");
```

##### Do

```js
const { execFile } = require("child_process");
execFile("convert", [name, "out.png"]);
```

#### JSX

##### Don't

```jsx
const { exec } = require("child_process");
exec("convert " + name + " out.png");
```

##### Do

```jsx
const { execFile } = require("child_process");
execFile("convert", [name, "out.png"]);
```

#### TypeScript

##### Don't

```ts
const { exec } = require("child_process");
exec("convert " + name + " out.png");
```

##### Do

```ts
const { execFile } = require("child_process");
execFile("convert", [name, "out.png"]);
```

#### TSX

##### Don't

```tsx
const { exec } = require("child_process");
exec("convert " + name + " out.png");
```

##### Do

```tsx
const { execFile } = require("child_process");
execFile("convert", [name, "out.png"]);
```

## `sec-js/no-cleartext-http` — No request made over http://

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-security-js` · `codelaw-rules-security-js` · **Languages:** JavaScript, JSX, TypeScript, TSX
- **Fix:** `manual` (the server must answer on HTTPS before the scheme is switched, and the text of a URL cannot be rewritten by an edit primitive)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:sec-js/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-js/strict` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-ts/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-ts/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/sec-js/no-cleartext-http.md

### What it checks

`fetch`, `axios`, `http.get`, `got` and similar are not given a literal `http://` URL, other than for localhost.

**Why:** A request over plain HTTP can be read and rewritten by anyone on the network path, including the credentials and tokens in it (CWE-319).

### How to fix

1. Change `http://` to `https://` in the URL, and check the server answers on it.
2. Where the host has no certificate, get one (Let's Encrypt) rather than falling back to HTTP.
3. A URL that is only ever local (`localhost`, `127.0.0.1`) may stay; those are not flagged.

### Examples

#### JavaScript

##### Don't

```js
const response = await fetch("http://api.example-bank.com/accounts");
```

##### Do

```js
const response = await fetch("https://api.example-bank.com/accounts");
```

#### JSX

##### Don't

```jsx
const response = await fetch("http://api.example-bank.com/accounts");
```

##### Do

```jsx
const response = await fetch("https://api.example-bank.com/accounts");
```

#### TypeScript

##### Don't

```ts
const response = await fetch("http://api.example-bank.com/accounts");
```

##### Do

```ts
const response = await fetch("https://api.example-bank.com/accounts");
```

#### TSX

##### Don't

```tsx
const response = await fetch("http://api.example-bank.com/accounts");
```

##### Do

```tsx
const response = await fetch("https://api.example-bank.com/accounts");
```

## `sec-js/no-cors-wildcard-credentials` — No CORS that allows every origin together with credentials

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-security-js` · `codelaw-rules-security-js` · **Languages:** JavaScript, JSX, TypeScript, TSX
- **Fix:** `manual` (which origins may call the API is a decision for the author)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:sec-js/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-js/strict` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-ts/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-ts/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/sec-js/no-cors-wildcard-credentials.md

### What it checks

`cors()` is not given `origin: "*"` or `origin: true` together with `credentials: true`.

**Why:** `origin: true` reflects whatever origin asks, so any website can send the visitor's cookies to your API and read the answer (CWE-942).

### How to fix

1. List the origins that may call the API: `origin: ["https://app.example.com"]`, or a function that checks a list.
2. Drop `credentials: true` if the API does not use cookies; then `origin: "*"` is acceptable for public data.

### Examples

#### JavaScript

##### Don't

```js
app.use(cors({ origin: true, credentials: true }));
```

##### Do

```js
app.use(cors({ origin: ["https://app.example.com"], credentials: true }));
```

#### JSX

##### Don't


##### Do


#### TypeScript

##### Don't

#### TSX


##### Do


## `sec-js/no-csrf-before-method-override` — No method-override before the CSRF check

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-security-js` · `codelaw-rules-security-js` · **Languages:** JavaScript, JSX, TypeScript, TSX

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-security-js` · `codelaw-rules-security-js` · **Languages:** JavaScript, JSX, TypeScript, TSX
- **Fix:** `manual` (whether the value needs markup at all is a decision for the author)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:sec-js/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-js/strict` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-ts/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-ts/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/sec-js/no-dangerously-set-inner-html.md

### What it checks

React's `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` is given a literal, or a value that went through a sanitizer such as `DOMPurify.sanitize`.

**Your sanitizer:** a value passes when it is a call to one of the `sanitizers`: the built-in list (DOMPurify, sanitize-html, xss, escape-html, lodash and he `escape`, Trusted Types `createHTML`) plus your own, each matched by name and by the module it is imported from, so a local `function sanitize(x) { return x }` does not pass. `sanitizers_mode = "replace"` makes yours the only ones that count. It does not follow a value through a variable: `const c = clean(x)` then `c` at the sink is not a call. Add a project function with `sanitizers = [{ name = "sanitizeHtml", module = "@acme/security" }]`.

**Why:** The name is the warning: the value becomes the element's HTML, so markup an attacker supplies runs in the page (CWE-79).

### Options

| Option | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sanitizers` | `call[]` | 10 entries (below) | functions whose result may reach the sink: a callee path (global) or { name, module }; `sanitizers_mode: replace` makes them the only ones that count |
| `sanitizers_mode` | `string` | `"extend"` | `extend` adds your `sanitizers` to the default list; `replace` uses only yours |

### How to fix

1. Render the value as text (`{comment.body}`) wherever it need not carry markup.
2. Where it must, pass it through a sanitizer first: `DOMPurify.sanitize(html)`, and keep the allowed tags narrow.
3. Sanitize once, at the edge, and keep the sanitized string in its own variable so the call is next to the use.

### Examples

#### JavaScript

##### Don't

```js
const props = { dangerouslySetInnerHTML: { __html: comment.body } };
```

##### Do

```js
const props = { dangerouslySetInnerHTML: { __html: DOMPurify.sanitize(comment.body) } };
```

#### JSX

##### Don't

```jsx
const props = { dangerouslySetInnerHTML: { __html: comment.body } };
```

##### Do

```jsx
const props = { dangerouslySetInnerHTML: { __html: DOMPurify.sanitize(comment.body) } };
```

#### TypeScript

##### Don't

```ts
const props = { dangerouslySetInnerHTML: { __html: comment.body } };
```

##### Do

```ts
const props = { dangerouslySetInnerHTML: { __html: DOMPurify.sanitize(comment.body) } };
```

#### TSX

##### Don't

```tsx
const props = { dangerouslySetInnerHTML: { __html: comment.body } };
```

##### Do

```tsx
const props = { dangerouslySetInnerHTML: { __html: DOMPurify.sanitize(comment.body) } };
```

## `sec-js/no-document-cookie-token` — No token or session written to document.cookie

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-security-js` · `codelaw-rules-security-js` · **Languages:** JavaScript, JSX, TypeScript, TSX
- **Fix:** `manual` (the cookie has to be set by the server, which is a change to the response)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:sec-js/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-js/strict` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-ts/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-ts/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/sec-js/no-document-cookie-token.md

### What it checks

A token, a session id or a password is not written to `document.cookie`; the server sets it with `Set-Cookie`.

**Why:** A cookie script can write is a cookie script can read, so it has no `HttpOnly` flag, and any XSS reads it (CWE-1004).

### How to fix

1. Return the credential in the response and let the server send `Set-Cookie: token=…; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax`.
2. Keep the cookie out of script's reach: the page calls the API and the browser attaches the cookie.

### Examples

#### JavaScript

##### Don't

```js
document.cookie = "token=" + token + "; path=/";
```

##### Do

```js
document.cookie = "theme=dark; path=/";
```

#### JSX

##### Don't

```jsx
document.cookie = "token=" + token + "; path=/";
```

##### Do

```jsx
document.cookie = "theme=dark; path=/";
```

#### TypeScript

##### Don't

```ts
document.cookie = "token=" + token + "; path=/";
```

##### Do

```ts
document.cookie = "theme=dark; path=/";
```

#### TSX

##### Don't

```tsx
document.cookie = "token=" + token + "; path=/";
```

##### Do

```tsx
document.cookie = "theme=dark; path=/";
```

## `sec-js/no-dynamic-script-src` — No script or frame source taken from a value that is not a literal

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-security-js` · `codelaw-rules-security-js` · **Languages:** JavaScript, JSX, TypeScript, TSX

- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:sec-js/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-js/strict` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-ts/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-ts/strict` at `error`

### What it checks

The `src` of a `<script>`, `<iframe>`, `<frame>` or `<embed>` element is not set from a value that is not a literal.

**Why:** A script source the page computes is code it loads and runs; a value an attacker influences loads code of their choosing (CWE-829).
